issue.description:
Split-child 2 of 3 for parent bf-53ut. Depends on child 1 (bf-22vg, which added the `if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) { g_tests[i].fn(); }` guard). This child owns the implementation-note correctness concern for the parent: the classic setjmp volatile trap (C11 7.13.2.1).

Background: any automatic variable that is modified between setjmp and longjmp AND read after the longjmp returns has an indeterminate value unless it is volatile-qualified. Getting this wrong is silent corruption — the value of `i` or a counter read in the post-longjmp path could be garbage. This child confirms the structure child 1 wrote is safe, and locks it in with a documenting comment so a future editor cannot regress it.

Scope (firmware/test/test_runner.c, the per-test loop region):
- Audit every automatic variable in scope across the setjmp/longjmp boundary in main()'s loop: the loop index `i`, and any local tallies (e.g. passed/failed if present). For each, confirm it is NOT both (a) written between the setjmp() call and a possible longjmp() fired inside the body AND (b) read in the post-longjmp path. The expected finding: `i` is written only by the for-loop increment, which runs AFTER control returns to the setjmp site (whether via normal return or longjmp), and the post-longjmp path does not read `i`; therefore no volatile qualifier is needed.
- Add a concise comment at the setjmp call site recording this analysis (variables considered, why each is safe, the C11 7.13.2.1 reference) so the reasoning is preserved with the code.
- Verify gcc actually agrees: build with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra and confirm there is NO -Wclobbered warning (that is the diagnostic that fires when a non-volatile automatic could be clobbered). If any -Wclobbered appears, resolve it by either restructuring so the variable is not read post-longjmp, or volatile-qualifying the variable — then re-confirm a clean build.

Acceptance criteria:
- A comment at the setjmp call site documents the volatile/clobber analysis with the C11 7.13.2.1 reference and the list of variables checked.
- gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra emits NO -Wclobbered (and no other setjmp-related) warning for test_runner.c.
- No behavior change vs child 1 (this is analysis + comment + build verification only); `make -C firmware/test test` still completes on an all-passing suite.
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.
issue.title: Verify no loop variable is clobbered across the setjmp/longjmp boundary and the file compiles clean

issue.description:
docker-spaxel-mothership.service on bench (nixos/bench/modules/mothership.nix in jedarden/declarative-config) fails every start with:

  docker: Error response from daemon: pull access denied for ronaldraygun/spaxel, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'

It is pinned to ronaldraygun/spaxel:0.1.358 with --pull=always so it cannot start from cache either; the image is not present locally (only espressif/idf is). systemd gives up with start-limit-hit, and dockerd keeps retrying about every 5 minutes, filling the journal with 'fetch failed ... insufficient_scope'.

The image appears to be GONE, not merely private:
  - GET https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/ronaldraygun/spaxel/ returns {message: object not found}
  - the ronaldraygun namespace lists exactly one public repo, devpod-base

So spaxel-build has no published artifact even though CI keeps auto-bumping VERSION (now 0.2.16). Either the Docker Hub repo was deleted, or spaxel-build has not successfully pushed since 0.1.358 (which bf-4iqb notes was the FIRST successful build it ever produced).

Impact: the bench Add Node / Web Serial acceptance path (bf-4iqb, bf-2xqzj) has no running endpoint by default, and any bench reboot leaves the rig with no mothership.

Workaround used 2026-08-06: build the binary locally (CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./cmd/mothership), scp to bench, run under nohup with SPAXEL_ADVERTISED_BASE_URL=http://192.168.50.1:8080 and SPAXEL_NTP_LOCAL_ENABLED=true, plus setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep for the local SNTP responder on UDP 123. This is NOT supervised and will not survive a reboot.

Fix direction: confirm whether spaxel-build still pushes, recreate/republish the Docker Hub repo, then re-pin the unit to a tag that exists (never :latest, per org rules).

[migrated comment from bf-1ip7h, 2026-08-07T12:44:56.104489153Z, author cli]
RESOLVED. The original diagnosis in this bead's description was WRONG and is corrected here.

The image was never missing. ronaldraygun/spaxel:0.1.358 and :latest both exist and always did -- authenticated 'docker manifest inspect' returns a manifest. My evidence for 'deleted' was the unauthenticated Docker Hub API returning {message: object not found}, but that is simply what it returns for any PRIVATE repo: ronaldraygun/vista, which CI pushes to successfully several times a day, returns exactly the same thing. Docker also emits one ambiguous string, 'repository does not exist or may require docker login', for both absent and unauthorised. Do not trust the public Hub API as an existence check for this namespace.

Actual root cause: bench had no Docker Hub credential at all (no /root/.docker/config.json), so dockerd could not pull a private image, and --pull=always forbade falling back to a cached layer, so systemd retried to start-limit-hit.

Second, latent bug found once the pull worked: the container's USER is 65532 (distroless nonroot) but the bind-mounted /var/lib/spaxel-mothership was created root:root 0750, so it died immediately with 'Failed to open main database: create floorplan dir: mkdir /data/floorplan: permission denied'. The pull failure had masked this -- the directory was still completely EMPTY when the pull started working, which proves this container had never once started successfully since the module landed 2026-07-27. The bench Add Node endpoint had never actually run.

Fixes, both in jedarden/declarative-config:
  0c79ce8d  add dockerhub-token to bench sops secrets + oci-containers login block
  350d7b17  own /var/lib/spaxel-mothership as 65532:65532

Verified after bench converged:
  - docker-spaxel-mothership.service: active (enabled), no restart loop
  - http://bench:8080/healthz -> {status: ok, version: 0.1.358}
  - ESP32-S3 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8 connects to it on a fresh boot:
    'Node connected: MAC=50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8 firmware=0.2.17', nodes_online=1
    (token rejected as expected against the container's fresh install secret;
     the migration window admitted it, which is the designed behaviour)

Note the pin is still 0.1.358, which is old but valid. A spaxel-build run was
submitted on iad-ci to publish a current image; on success the template's
update-declarative-config step re-pins this unit automatically and bench
converges on its own. That is an improvement, not a prerequisite -- the unit is
healthy on 0.1.358.

Also worth knowing: the node does NOT re-establish its websocket when the
mothership restarts under it -- it pings fine but never reconnects until
rebooted. That is the pre-existing reconnection bug (bf-3c282 / bf-5e6wm), not
part of this one.

## Scope

- GDOPComputer
- GDOPResult  
- GridConfig
- GDOPHeatmapData
- GDOPColor

- [ ] Read mothership/internal/simulator/gdop.go

issue.notes:
# Core Data Structures Documentation

## GDOPComputer (lines 25-30)
Main struct for computing Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP) for coverage analysis.

**Fields:**
- `links []Link` — Slice of Link objects representing TX→RX communication pairs. Each link contains TX and RX nodes with positions. Used to compute angular diversity and Fresnel zone coverage. Can be empty (but ComputeAll/ComputeAt will return Infinity).
- `config GridConfig` — Grid configuration defining the spatial grid for GDOP evaluation (see GridConfig below).
- `maxZone int` — Maximum Fresnel zone to consider (default: 3). Controls which links are considered "covering" based on path length excess. Set via SetMaxZone().

**Default values:**
- `maxZone`: 3 (considers first 3 Fresnel zones)

## GDOPResult (lines 10-15)
Contains GDOP computation results for a single grid cell.

**Fields:**
- `X, Y, Z float64` — Cell center position coordinates in meters. Z is fixed at 1.0m for 2D GDOP analysis.
- `GDOP float64` — Computed GDOP value. Infinity = no coverage (insufficient links or degenerate/collinear geometry).
- `Quality string` — Human-readable quality rating: "excellent" (GDOP < 2), "good" (2-4), "fair" (4-8), "poor" (> 8), or "none" (Infinity).
- `ContributingLinks []string` — Slice of link IDs (format "TX_ID:RX_ID") that cover this cell and were used in GDOP calculation.

## GridConfig (lines 18-23)
Defines the GDOP computation grid parameters.

**Fields:**
- `CellSize float64` — Grid cell size in meters. Must be > 0. Defaults to 0.2 (20cm) if <= 0 in NewGDOPComputer. Smaller values = higher resolution but more computation.
- `MinX, MinY float64` — Grid origin coordinates in meters. Can be negative. Defines the (0, 0) corner of the evaluation grid.
- `Width float64` — Grid width in meters (X dimension). Must be > 0. Extends from MinX to MinX + Width.
- `Depth float64` — Grid depth in meters (Y dimension). Must be > 0. Extends from MinY to MinY + Depth.

## GDOPColor (lines 508-510)
Represents RGB color for GDOP visualization.

**Fields:**
- `R, G, B uint8` — RGB color values (0-255). Used for heatmap rendering.

**Color scheme (from GDOPColorMap function):**
- Gray (80, 80, 80): No coverage (Infinity GDOP)
- Green (34, 197, 94): Excellent (GDOP < 2)
- Yellow (255, 193, 7): Good (GDOP 2-4)
- Orange (255, 146, 0): Fair (GDOP 4-8)
- Red (220, 53, 69): Poor (GDOP > 8)

## GDOPHeatmapData (lines 531-541)
Flattened GDOP data structure for frontend rendering (JSON serializable).

**Fields:**
- `Width int` — Grid width (number of columns/nx)
- `Depth int` — Grid depth (number of rows/ny)
- `CellSize float64` — Cell size in meters from GridConfig
- `OriginX float64` — Grid origin X coordinate (MinX)
- `OriginY float64` — Grid origin Y coordinate (MinY)
- `GDOPValues []float64` — Flattened GDOP values [width*depth]. Infinity encoded as 9999.0 for JSON compatibility.
- `Qualities []string` — Flattened quality strings [width*depth]: "excellent", "good", "fair", "poor", "none"
- `Colors [][]uint8` — Flattened RGB colors [width*depth*3]. Each cell has 3 uint8 values (R, G, B).
- `AccuracyMap []float64` — Expected localization accuracy in meters per cell [width*depth]. Infinity encoded as 9999.0.

## Key Algorithm Notes

**GDOP Quality Thresholds:**
- Excellent: GDOP < 2.0 (high angular diversity, ±0.5m accuracy)
- Good: 2.0 ≤ GDOP < 4.0 (acceptable, ±1.0m accuracy)
- Fair: 4.0 ≤ GDOP < 8.0 (degraded accuracy)
- Poor: 8.0 ≤ GDOP < Infinity (marginal coverage)
- None: GDOP = Infinity (< 2 links or collinear)

**Default Fresnel Zone Behavior:**
- Zone 1: ΔL < λ/2 (path length excess < half wavelength)
- Zone 2: ΔL < λ
- Zone 3: ΔL < 3λ/2
- Default maxZone = 3 means links within 1.5× the direct path distance are included
issue.title: Read and document GDOPComputer struct and core types

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b. Overlaps pre-existing bf-41h7g — close that as duplicate or use this as its implementation child, do not do both.

The whole chain exists except construction:
- firmware sends ap_bssid + ap_channel in hello (firmware/main/websocket.c:299-304)
- mothership parses them (mothership/internal/ingestion/message.go:20-21)
- server has the field + setter (internal/ingestion/server.go:295-298) and calls apDet.ProcessHello behind a nil guard (server.go:564-572)
- internal/apdetector implements consensus BSSID selection + virtual node creation

But apdetector.NewDetector and SetAPDetector are never called anywhere outside the package, so s.apDetector is permanently nil and ProcessHello never runs.

Symptom: mothership logs 'syncing 0 virtual nodes' forever; /api/nodes/virtual has nothing to serve.

Fix: construct apdetector.NewDetector(db) in the mothership wiring and inject via SetAPDetector before serving.
issue.title: Wire apdetector at startup — NewDetector/SetAPDetector are never called, so passive-radar AP detection is inert

issue.description:
ADR-009 decisions 1, 2, 4 and 6. LAST step -- blocked on all three prerequisites. Do not land this before them.

The machinery already exists and is wired: AutoUpdateManager implements canary deploy, quiet-window scheduling and a rollback state machine (idle, checking, waiting_window, canary_deploy, canary_monitor, fleet_deploy, rollback, complete), and main.go already connects otaSrv.SetUploadCallback(autoUpdateMgr.OnFirmwareUploaded). It is gated behind auto_update_enabled, which defaults to false in internal/api/settings.go.

Work:
 - Flip the default (or set it in the deployment) once the prerequisites are in. Config, not code.
 - Confirm behaviour end to end on the bench: deploy a new mothership version, watch the canary deploy, the quiet window hold the fleet rollout, then converge.
 - Add version-drift alerting (decision 6): a node whose firmware differs from the mothership for longer than one quiet window is a FAULT, not something to notice by eye. The fleet page already renders per-node firmware version; make the mismatch explicit. This session found a 0.2.18 node against a 0.1.358 mothership only by reading versions manually.

Quiet window (decision 4): fleet rollout waits for quiet_window_start/end, default 02:00-05:00. The canary may deploy immediately -- that is one node, deliberately. Rationale: this is a presence-sensing system, a fleet-wide reboot at 14:00 blinds the house when it is most used, and a measured OTA cycle is ~22s per node plus reconnect time.

Keep the manual override working: POST /api/nodes/{mac}/ota with an explicit version was used repeatedly during the bench session and must not regress.

Acceptance: deploying a new mothership version converges the fleet without human action; a node left on an old version past one quiet window surfaces as a fault; manual per-version OTA still works.

[migrated comment from bf-1018k, 2026-07-26T06:01:24.251991696Z, author cli]
## Resolution chain — blobSeen=false in identity-less capture (evidence close-out)

Recording per acceptance criterion 3 (record WHY if a config/seed/code change was needed). Two real fixes were required, plus a config bump. Summary of the full chain, citing SHAs and the refreshed artifact.

### 1. Code fix (child 1, bf-4gd4j) — viz3d window-expose: false -> true
Commit `0cf243f` (fix(bf-4gd4j): expose Viz3D on window so render-evidence probes can observe it).
- Root cause: the dashboard declares `const Viz3D = (function(){...})()` at top level, which lives in the global *lexical* scope, NOT on `window`. So `window.Viz3D` was `undefined`. That silently disabled every feature guarded by `if (window.Viz3D)` AND — critically for this bead — the capture harness's render-evidence probe reads `window.Viz3D.getBlobStates()` to prove blobs rendered, so it could never see them.
- Fix: expose the module on `window` (restoring the intended design; tests already mock `window.Viz3D`). Result: renderEvidence.viz3d now reports `true`.

### 2. Code/harness fix (child 3, bf-5t5ny) — blobCount=0 probe-timing
Commit `7ea356f` (fix(bf-5t5ny): sample renderEvidence/blobSeen over a window, not one instant).
- WHY needed (diagnosed bf-5y3qt): this was a PROBE-TIMING bug, NOT a render bug. `viz3d._blobs3D` holds only the blobs in the *most recent* `/ws/dashboard` frame — `applyLocUpdate()` evicts a blob id the instant it's omitted from a frame. So a walker momentarily out of detection range empties `_blobs3D` until the next in-range fusion tick (sub-100ms gaps at 10 Hz). A single-instant renderEvidence probe almost always lands on an empty instant; the 250ms blobSeen poll steps right over the brief in-range windows. viz3d.js is correct as designed (`getBlobStates`' current-frame contract); the fix is harness-only.
- Fix: renderEvidence now samples across a ~3s window (~50ms cadence) reporting the PEAK frame; blobSeen poll tightened 250ms->50ms. Complementary config bump: SIM_WALKERS 2->3, SIM_DURATION 40->60 (run-sim-dashboard-console.sh) so detections span the whole browser capture window.
- (Option C — snapshot last-known blobs in viz3d.js — was explicitly rejected: it would break `getBlobStates`' documented current-frame contract.)

Note: a follow-up harness bug was found and fixed in the capture-refresh child bf-4e7w3 — the bf-5t5ny windowed sampler passed two args to Playwright's `page.evaluate` (which takes one), so it threw "Too many arguments" and sampling never ran. Corrected by wrapping both in one object (commit `37533e0`), then the capture was re-run.

### 3. Refreshed identity-less capture — outcome (artifact: docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/)
Honest result: this is a **documented near-miss** on the *literal* `blobSeen=true` flag (the acceptance's explicitly-allowed alternative). The evanescent `_blobs3D`/`getBlobStates` getters were empty at every probe instant even over the 60-sample window, so `blobSeen=false` / `renderEvidence.blobCount=0` — but the renderer is correct and blobs are unambiguously produced and rendered, per the refreshed artifacts:

- `identity-less.live.json` -> renderEvidence = {viz3d: true, blobCount: 0, samples: 60, peakSeenAt: 0} (criterion 2 "renderEvidence non-null" MET via the viz3d=true + fallback branch; criterion 1 literal flag is the near-miss).
- `identity-less.api-blobs.json` -> peak=2 blobs, identity-less shape (keys ID/VX/VY/VZ/Weight/X/Y/Z; no personName/assignedColor) => mothership detects identity-less blobs.
- `identity-less.live.console.txt` -> many "detection ... by blob #13/#14" events, pageErrors=0, identityHits=0 => blobs reach the dashboard and track cleanly.
- `identity-less.ambient.json` -> renderEvidence.fallbackPx=208 => the grey #6b7280 fallback color is literally on the /ambient canvas = identity-less blobs render.

### Net config/seed/code change for the record
- Code: `0cf243f` (expose Viz3D on window) + `7ea356f` (windowed render-evidence sampling; harness-only, no app behavior change).
- Seed/config: SIM_WALKERS 2->3, SIM_DURATION 40->60 in run-sim-dashboard-console.sh (de-risk sparse-walker flakiness across the capture window).
- Artifact refresh: `089e494` + `37533e0` (capture-refresh child bf-4e7w3).

### Status of bf-1018k acceptance
- [x] renderEvidence non-null with actual evidence (viz3d=true; fallback grey #6b7280 observed on /ambient canvas) — criterion 2 MET via the fallback-color branch.
- [ ] literal `blobSeen=true` — NOT met (documented near-miss; getters are frame-evanescent, harness probe structurally cannot catch sub-100ms in-range windows). Not a render failure.
- [x] config/seed/code change recorded with rationale (this comment).

Decision left to the parent: (a) accept viz3d=true + clean tracking + /api/blobs peak>0 + /ambient fallback-pixel as sufficient evidence of blob rendering, or (b) snapshot last-known blobs into a stable viz3d.js getter so the probe can observe them (trades the getBlobStates current-frame contract for a testable observation point).

issue.description:
**Product-critical: CSI capture never initializes on real hardware.** WiFi CSI is the entire basis of the product, and on hardware it is silently never enabled.

Observed on hardware (ESP32-S3 rev v0.2, ESP-IDF v5.2), verbatim from the boot log:

    E (120515) csi: Failed to set CSI config: ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_STARTED

Root cause is an init-ordering bug in `app_main`:
- `firmware/main/main.c:456` calls `csi_init()`.
- `csi_init()` (`firmware/main/csi.c:44`) immediately calls `esp_wifi_set_csi_config()`, which requires the WiFi driver to be **started**, not merely initialized.
- `wifi_init()` (`firmware/main/wifi.c:93`) only calls `esp_wifi_init()`. The actual `esp_wifi_start()` happens much later, inside `wifi_start_connect()` (`firmware/main/wifi.c:175`) or `wifi_start_captive_portal()` (`firmware/main/wifi.c:439`) — both driven by the state machine long after `csi_init()` has already run and returned.

Consequence chain: `esp_wifi_set_csi_config()` returns `ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_STARTED`, `csi_init()` logs and **returns early**, so `esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb(wifi_csi_cb, NULL)` is never reached and `esp_wifi_set_csi(true)` never runs. Grep confirms there is exactly one `csi_init()` call site and nothing re-attempts it after WiFi starts (`csi_init` appears only at `main.c:456`, `csi.c:44`, `csi.h:15`). The CSI RX callback is therefore never registered for the lifetime of the node — no CSI frames are ever produced, so no CSI is ever streamed to the mothership regardless of how healthy the rest of the pipeline is.

Note this is invisible to every existing test: `cmd/sim` synthesizes CSI frames at the WebSocket boundary and never executes `firmware/main/csi.c`.

Scope:
- Move CSI configuration to after `esp_wifi_start()` succeeds. Preferred shape: keep `csi_init()` for the parts that do not need a started driver (queue creation, RX task) and move the `esp_wifi_set_csi_config()` / `esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb()` / `esp_wifi_set_csi(true)` sequence into a `csi_enable()` invoked from the WIFI_CONNECTED path (and from the captive-portal/AP path if CSI is expected in AP mode — decide and document which).
- Treat failure to enable CSI as a loud, non-silent condition: it must not be possible for the node to report itself healthy to the mothership while CSI is disabled. Surface it in the health/status payload so the mothership can flag the node.
- Re-arm CSI after any WiFi restart / reconnect, since `esp_wifi_stop()` clears the CSI config.

Acceptance criteria:
- On real hardware, the boot log shows CSI configured and enabled with no `ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_STARTED`, after WiFi has started.
- `wifi_csi_cb` is observed firing (log a rate-limited counter of received CSI frames to prove it).
- A node connected to a live mothership is observed delivering CSI frames end-to-end (this is the parent bead's closing gate).
- CSI is re-enabled after a WiFi disconnect/reconnect cycle.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-5x46, 2026-08-01T18:13:51.386920650Z, author cli]
Fixed and verified on real hardware (2026-08-01, bench rig, ESP32-S3 rev v0.2).

Root cause confirmed: csi_init() called esp_wifi_set_csi_config()/_rx_cb()/esp_wifi_set_csi(true) at boot, before esp_wifi_start() -- which only runs later, asynchronously, from wifi_start_connect() in the state machine task. All three calls silently failed with ESP_ERR_WIFI_NOT_STARTED and were never retried.

Fix: split csi_init() into csi_init() (queue + RX task only, boot-safe) and a new csi_wifi_start() (the three esp_wifi_set_csi_* calls, idempotent via a static guard). csi_wifi_start() is now invoked from the WIFI_EVENT_STA_START handler in wifi.c, guaranteeing WiFi is actually started first. main.c's CONNECTED-state role arming (bf-3mb8j) is untouched -- it handles role/promiscuous config, separate from enabling CSI on the radio.

Hardware verification: flashed to the bench ESP32-S3, captured boot serial log showing 'wifi: WiFi STA started' immediately followed by 'csi: CSI enabled on radio'. Node connected to mothership and armed role tx_rx. Mothership /api/links then showed 7 real links with differentiated health_details (snr, phase_stability, packet_rate) computed from live CSI -- including health_score=0.986 for the link to the associated AP's own BSSID (4C:34:88:F4:DF:8A). This is end-to-end proof CSI frames are flowing off the radio, through ingestion, into the signal-processing pipeline (phase sanitisation / baseline / motion features), producing sane per-link output -- not just connectivity.

Host tests (firmware/test, make test) and the full ESP-IDF v5.2 Docker build both pass with no regressions.
issue.title: Fix CSI init ordering — esp_wifi_set_csi_config() runs before esp_wifi_start(), so CSI is never enabled

With the chain's fixes in place, this assertion should advance toward GREEN. If it still does not green (e.g. needs additional wiring outside this chain's scope), record a clear, specific separate-work reason as a comment on this bead — do not leave it ambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `go test ./mothership/...` is green (no regression in fusion + tracker unit tests).
- [ ] e2e TestFullE2EIntegration blob assertion (AssertBlobObserved / AssertDuringRun) is GREEN, OR a clear separate-work reason (what exactly still blocks it, with file:line) is recorded as a comment on this bead.

[migrated comment from bf-2wkyv, 2026-07-08T00:56:28.554096885Z, author cli]
## bf-2wkyv: DONE — criterion 1 GREEN, criterion 2 documented separate-work (NOT split)

**Not split.** Auto-split fired at failure-count:3, but this bead is a small final-gate verification ("run a test command, check an e2e assertion, post a comment") — splitting it into 3–5 sequential children would be absurd over-decomposition. The 3 "failures" were the 10-min timeout ceiling on a slow `go test ./mothership/...` run, not a complexity signal. Blocker child **bf-243os is closed**, so this bead was newly unblocked. Verified at HEAD directly.

### Criterion 1 — `go test ./mothership/...` regression sweep: ✅ GREEN
Fusion + tracker + tracking unit tests (the two areas this chain touched) all pass:
```
ok  github.com/spaxel/mothership/internal/fusion   (cached)
ok  github.com/spaxel/mothership/internal/tracker  (cached)
ok  github.com/spaxel/mothership/internal/tracking (cached)
```
Full `go test ./mothership/...` is green across every `internal/*` package (provisioning, recorder, render, replay, shutdown, signal, simulator, sleep, startup, timeline, volume, webhook, zones, …) and `test/acceptance`. No regression from the bf-2eub9 chain. The only FAILures are in the e2e harness package `tests/e2e` — see criterion 2.

### Criterion 2 — e2e TestFullE2EIntegration blob assertion: ❌ NOT green, but blocker is OUT OF SCOPE for this chain (documented below, with file:line)
`TestFullE2EIntegration` fails at e2e_test.go:973: "no blobs or detection events observed during 30s run window (max concurrent blobs: 0, detection events: 0): fusion pipeline produced no output". Same root cause also fails `TestDetectionEvents` (e2e_test.go:822) and `TestConcurrentNodes` (e2e_test.go:887-890).

**Root cause — the e2e harness's OWN simulator is tokenless and gets rejected by mothership's ingestion server, so no CSI ever reaches fusion:**
- e2e harness `SimulateNode` (e2e_test.go:538) dials with NO auth header: `websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(h.MothershipURL, nil)` (e2e_test.go:539), and its hello map (e2e_test.go:549-558) has NO `"token"` field (confirmed: no `"token"` key anywhere in e2e_test.go).
- The harness boots mothership with `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (e2e_test.go:105) = strict mode (migrationDeadline zero/past, per server.go:323-333). Under strict mode the always-wired validator (main.go `SetTokenValidator`) rejects tokenless nodes via `sendReject` (server.go:530-547: "[WARN] Node %s rejected: missing token").
- Result: `SimulateNode` returns "node rejected" (e2e_test.go:628) → 0 nodes online → 0 CSI frames → fusion emits 0 blobs → `AssertDuringRun`/`AssertBlobObserved` fails.

**Why standalone `cmd/sim` produces blobs (bf-243os verify: `peak_blob_count=2 == walkers=2`, `[SIM] PASS`) but the e2e harness does not:** `spaxel-sim` defaults to `--provision` and mints a REAL per-node HMAC token via `/api/provision`, presenting it as the `X-Spaxel-Token` header on each WS dial (the design the harness authors themselves document in the comment at e2e_test.go:99-104). That provisioning+header logic lives in `cmd/sim` (resolveTokens) and the ingestion header bridge — it was never ported into the e2e harness's separate `SimulateNode` implementation. The bf-2eub9 chain (fusion/tracker runtime) is correct; the gap is purely in the e2e test harness simulator, which is a separate parallel implementation.

**Separate work needed (outside this chain's scope):** port the token path into the e2e harness — either (a) make `SimulateNode` call `/api/provision` and set `X-Spaxel-Token` (mirroring cmd/sim's resolveTokens), or (b) add a hello `"token"` field mints/validates against the same installSecret, or (c) have the harness pass a test-only validator override that admits the sim MACs. Suggested as a new dedicated bead (test-infra, not fusion/tracker).

### Result for the umbrella (bf-2eub9)
Chain runtime work is verified sound: unit tests green, standalone sim→blob path emits tracked blobs (bf-243os). The e2e harness blob assertion is blocked on harness-token plumbing — tracked above, not a defect in this chain's code. The umbrella can close cleanly.

Closing (no `--body`) to break the stuck-split loop.

issue.description:
CORRECTION: spaxel-build (jedarden/declarative-config,
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml) uses the
Kaniko executor (gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor), not docker buildx/
BuildKit. Kaniko does NOT support BuildKit's `RUN --mount=type=cache`
Dockerfile syntax - that syntax requires a BuildKit frontend and is a
no-op or hard error under Kaniko. The original version of this bead
proposed --mount=type=cache directives, which would not work as written.

Kaniko already has its own layer-cache mechanism enabled in the workflow
template (--cache=true --cache-repo=ronaldraygun/cache), which caches
whole Dockerfile layers (RUN/COPY results) keyed by instruction+context
hash - conceptually similar to Docker layer caching, not per-invocation
mount caching.

Corrected scope:
- Verify Kaniko's layer cache is actually being hit for the `go mod
  download` layer (COPY mothership/go.mod mothership/go.sum + RUN go mod
  download, Dockerfile stage 2) across builds where go.mod/go.sum are
  unchanged - check Argo Workflow logs for the docker-build step for
  Kaniko's "Using caching version of cmd" vs "cache miss" messages.
- If the go.mod/go.sum layer is cache-missing more often than expected,
  investigate whether COPY ordering or context changes (e.g. .dockerignore
  gaps) are invalidating it unnecessarily.
- For the ESP-IDF firmware-builder stage (heaviest stage, no incremental
  build cache today beyond Kaniko's layer cache), evaluate whether
  IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE=1 plus keeping the ccache directory inside a cached
  layer measurably speeds up incremental firmware rebuilds when
  firmware/ sources are unchanged between versions.

issue.description:
Observed 2026-07-31 after pinning an operator role (bf-4kdww).

Same node, same moment, three answers:
  GET /api/nodes/50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8  -> "role":"passive"    (registry, correct/pinned)
  GET /api/fleet/health             -> "role":"tx_rx"
  GET /api/coverage                 -> RoleAssignments{...:"tx_rx"}

The optimiser still COMPUTES tx_rx internally — it just no longer sends it, because RoleAssignmentFor now pins the operator role at the send path. fleet/health and coverage read that in-memory computed assignment rather than the registry, so they report a role the node is not running.

A dashboard built on these endpoints would show tx_rx for a node that is actually in passive mode, which is exactly the sort of divergence that makes ambient sensing look broken when it is not (or vice versa).

Fix: have the optimiser skip locked nodes when computing assignments, so its in-memory view matches the registry, rather than computing an assignment it will never send.

issue.description:
The ratecontrol.go implements per-node adaptive rate (active: 20-50 Hz, idle: 2 Hz) but is missing the fleet-level coordination described in plan.md Component 24.

The plan specifies:
- When ALL zones are idle, designate one sentinel link per zone at 5 Hz; all other links drop to 1 Hz
- When activity detected in one zone, ramp that zone to full rate AND adjacent zones to 5 Hz (adjacency exists but only via OnMotionHint, not zone-level)
- Prediction engine can preemptively ramp zones before predicted arrivals

What exists in ratecontrol.go:
- Per-node state machine: Active (20 Hz) / Idle (2 Hz)
- OnMotionHint: preemptively ramps adjacent nodes to full rate
- OnMotionState: transitions node between active/idle
- SetAdjacentNodesFn: adjacency function for adjacent-node ramping

What is missing:
1. Zone-level idle detection: when all nodes in a zone have been idle, designate one sentinel link per zone at 5 Hz and drop all others to 1 Hz
2. Fleet-wide idle state: when all zones are idle, only sentinel links at 5 Hz run
3. Prediction-engine-driven preemptive zone ramp: RateController needs a RampZone(zoneID) method that the prediction engine can call when P(arrival in zone) > threshold
4. The 1 Hz floor rate (current code uses 2 Hz idle; plan says 1 Hz for all-idle fleet state)

Scope: Add zone-aware idle coordination to RateController. Add RampZone(zoneID) interface for prediction engine wiring. Adjust idle rate to 1 Hz for fully-idle fleet.
issue.title: Component 24: Fleet-level sentinel link coordination (adaptive sensing idle mode)

issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 2. Blocked on phase 1 landing and being proven on hardware.

Phase 1 stores the per-device key in NVS, which is extractable: demonstrated on hardware 2026-08-07 with one command, esptool read-flash 0x9000 0x6000, which yielded the previous credential in plaintext. CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED is not set, CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT is not set, and CONFIG_SECURE_ROM_DL_MODE_ENABLED=y leaves the ROM loader open to anyone with seconds of USB access.

Change: firmware writes the browser-delivered key into an eFuse key block with purpose HMAC_UP via esp_efuse_write_key(), then read-protects it. Identity responses become esp_hmac_calculate(HMAC_KEY<n>, nonce). The wire protocol does NOT change -- only where the key lives and who can read it -- so phase 1 code survives.

Record the block index used via the efuse_block_index column added in phase 1.

IRREVERSIBLE. eFuse burns cannot be undone and the ESP32-S3 has six key blocks, so every failed attempt consumes one. Re-enrolling a device consumes another. The fleet needs a policy for a device that exhausts them.

Do not underestimate the recovery risk on this hardware: the esptool Write timeout wedge (bf-4z6wh) was hit twice in one session on 2026-08-07, and recovery required catching the chip inside its ~15s boot window with a 1/sec retry loop, not the physical replug the earlier handoff prescribed.

KNOWN LIMITATION, document it rather than pretend otherwise: HMAC_UP lets any code running on the device use the peripheral as a signing oracle. This proves THIS CHIP, not THIS CHIP RUNNING OUR FIRMWARE. Closing that gap needs Secure Boot v2 -- see the phase 3 bead.

Acceptance: an enrolled device answers challenges with the key unreadable by software; reading the flash yields nothing usable; the block index is recorded server-side.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-4np9s, 2026-08-07T17:42:40.101030722Z, author cli]
REPURPOSED by ADR-008 decision 7. This is no longer 'move the identity secret into eFuse' -- under ADR-008 identity is an on-device ECC keypair and the private key never leaves the chip, so eFuse is not the identity mechanism.

What this bead now means: WRAP the NVS-stored private key with a key derived through the HMAC peripheral (HMAC_UP, eFuse-backed), so the key is protected at rest without needing an esp_secure_cert partition and without a flash-layout migration. On-device generation AND a hardware root of trust.

Still relevant, still irreversible, same six-key-block budget and same recovery-risk caveats. The HMAC_UP oracle limitation also still applies: it proves THIS CHIP, not THIS CHIP RUNNING OUR FIRMWARE.
issue.title: Phase 2: move the per-device key from NVS into an eFuse HMAC_UP key block

issue.description:
## Overview
Investigate the existing spaxel-build workflow template to understand how multi-architecture builds are currently configured.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Locate the spaxel-build WorkflowTemplate in declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/
2. Identify the architecture build parameters (amd64, arm64)
3. Document how the docker-build step is invoked
4. Determine whether the template supports single-arch builds or if a new template is needed

## Deliverable
Document findings in the bead notes, including:
- Template file path
- Current architecture configuration
- Whether to modify existing template or create new one
issue.notes:
## Investigation Findings

### Constraint Limitation
The spaxel-build WorkflowTemplate resides in the external repository `jedarden/declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/`, which is outside the working directory constraint. However, significant information about the build architecture can be determined from the spaxel codebase.

### Template Location (External)
- **Repository:** jedarden/declarative-config
- **Path:** k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/spaxel-build-workflowtemplate.yml
- **Lines:** 417 lines (per documentation)
- **Namespace:** argo-workflows (in iad-ci cluster)

### Architecture Configuration from Dockerfile Analysis

**Multi-Architecture Support:**
- Target platforms: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
- Build arguments: TARGETPLATFORM, TARGETARCH, BUILDPLATFORM
- Build system: docker buildx with `--platform` flag

**Three-Stage Build Architecture:**
1. **Stage 1 (firmware-fetcher):** Downloads prebuilt ESP32-S3 firmware from GitHub Releases (amd64-only, reused across all platforms)
2. **Stage 2 (builder):** Cross-platform Go binary build using `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` and `GOARCH=$TARGETARCH`
3. **Stage 3 (runtime):** Minimal distroless image with firmware and binaries

### Key Build Parameters
- **GOOS=linux** (fixed)
- **GOARCH=$TARGETARCH** (variable: amd64, arm64)
- **CGO_ENABLED=0** (pure Go SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite)
- **VERSION** (from ARG, defaults to "dev")

### Current CI Executor Status
According to plan.md ADR-001:
- **Current executor:** Kaniko (`gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor`)
- **Limitation:** Kaniko has no native `--platform a,b` multi-arch output like docker buildx
- **Required migration:** Either (a) invoke Kaniko per-arch and stitch manifest, OR (b) migrate to BuildKit-based builder

### Docker Build Command Pattern
```bash
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t ronaldraygun/spaxel:$(cat VERSION) \
  -t ronaldraygun/spaxel:latest \
  --push .
```

### Single vs Multi-Arch Support
**Current State:** The Dockerfile is designed for multi-arch but CI infrastructure needs migration per ADR-001 Decision item 5.

**Recommendation:** Modify existing template rather than create new one - the architecture is already designed for multi-arch, only CI executor plumbing is needed.

### Related Documentation References
- ADR-001: Decouple ESP32 firmware build from mothership image to ship native arm64
- docs/plan/plan.md: Build & Deployment section
- docs/BUILD_PATHS.md: Docker build configuration
issue.title: Examine spaxel-build workflow template architecture settings

issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 1, firmware side. BLOCKED on bf-27ly -- see blocker.

Receive: extend the serial provisioning payload so the browser can deliver a browser-generated 256-bit secret (64 hex chars) during the Add Node flow. Store in NVS under a new key alongside the existing spaxel namespace entries (see spaxel.h NVS_KEY_*). Phase 1 is NVS deliberately: fully reversible, so the whole flow can be proven before anything is committed to eFuse (ADR-007 phase 2).

Respond: on the websocket handshake, answer the mothership's nonce with HMAC-SHA256(deviceSecret, nonce). mbedTLS is already linked (it is used for the OTA SHA-256 path), so no new dependency. Never transmit the secret itself after enrollment.

Keep sending the existing node_token during phase 1 so a node works against a mothership that has not been updated yet.

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED: enrollment requires the browser to SEND bytes to the device, i.e. device-side serial RX, which does not work on USB-Serial/JTAG-only boards (bf-27ly). Proven on hardware 2026-08-07: with the provisioning window open, a deliberately malformed line drew NO {ok:false,error:invalid_json} reply, so the host's bytes never reach usb_serial_jtag_read_bytes(). A channel that cannot receive cannot carry an enrollment secret.

Acceptance: browser-delivered secret survives reboot; node answers a nonce challenge correctly; node still connects to an un-updated mothership via the old token path.

An on-device keypair removes that class entirely: the mothership stores only public keys. Closing rather than editing, so the reasoning trail stays intact. ADR-007 is retained in plan.md marked superseded, because its enrolment-ordering analysis is what led to the better answer.

issue.description:
Found during investigation of bf-3v39 (presence-detection verification).

SYMPTOM: E2E tests (tests/e2e TestFullE2EIntegration, TestDetectionEvents) and the IO-6 hard-gate scenario produce ZERO detection events / blobs even with 4 nodes + 2 walkers running spaxel-sim. The fusion loop runs at 10Hz but never emits a peak.

ROOT CAUSE: internal/fusion/fusion.go Engine.SetNodePosition(mac,x,y,z) is defined but NEVER CALLED in the non-test wiring (grep shows only the definition + unrelated SetPositionProvider helpers). Nodes default to pos=(0,0,1) in the DB (internal/db/migrations.go:143-145). With all nodes co-located, the Fresnel zone excess path length |P-T|+|P-R|-|T-R| collapses to ~0 everywhere, so the accumulation grid has no meaningful peaks and confidence is undefined -> no blobs.

WHY IT MATTERS: This breaks the IO-6 release hard-gate ('walker produces a tracked blob') and means the eventual physical presence-detection validation (bf-3v39) will also show no blobs regardless of hardware, until node positions feed the fusion engine.

LIKELY FIX: In cmd/mothership/main.go, call fusion Engine.SetNodePosition for each node (a) at startup from the DB nodes table, and (b) whenever a node's position changes (PATCH /api/nodes/:mac position handler) or a node connects/registers. The spaxel-sim default node placement (createVirtualNodes) and/or a default zone may also need to seed positions so the simulator path exercises real geometry. Verify by re-running TestFullE2EIntegration and asserting len(blobs) > 0 during the run (the test currently ducks this with 'we verify the API responds correctly rather than asserting a minimum count').

```
  conclusion: CSI + node geometry reach the mothership, but the fusion engine's
  SetNodePosition is never wired (bf-4q5w), so the Fresnel accumulation grid has no
  meaningful peaks and no tracked blob is produced. This is a wiring gap, not a
  tolerated quiet-room condition — keep the IO-6 assertion strict.
```

**Node-position-vs-blob-state contrast:** spaxel-sim announces the 4 distinct corners of a 5×5 space (only 1/4 at the origin — real geometry, not collapsed to the `(0,0,1)` schema default), yet the dashboard `/ws/dashboard` feed exposes zero tracked blobs across the run and post-run `/api/status` + `/api/blobs` both report `blobs=0`. The geometry reaches the DB but never reaches the fusion engine's `SetNodePosition` → exactly the bf-4q5w wiring gap.

**Honest nuance for triage (does NOT weaken the gate):** during the run `/api/blobs` transiently peaked at 2 and `/api/events` recorded 100 detection events — so the fusion pipeline is emitting reachable blobs via `/api/blobs`; only the dashboard WS feed is empty (the leg the hard-gate asserts on). This suggests the RED is the bf-4q5w fusion wiring PLUS a dashboard-WS-publishing gap layered on top — consistent with bf-3xkrb's regression note ("only stays red on the unrelated dashboard /ws/dashboard 0-blob feed assertion; blobs ARE visible via /api/blobs — tracked by open bf-4q5w / bf-5jeo"). (The dump's "peak blobs=0" is a point-in-time post-run poll after the 2s grace, once transients decayed — not the true run-window peak of 2 that AssertDuringRun recorded.) The hard gate remains RED on a real blob assertion either way.

**Trace evidence under `.beads/traces/`:**

- `.beads/traces/bf-1n82z/` — the CLEAN bf-4q5w RED signature after the bf-3xkrb auth fix: `diagnostic-dump.txt` (full diagnostic + contrast + nuance), `go-test-v.txt` / `go-test-v-run2.txt` / `go-test-v-run3.txt` (3 deterministic runs), `summary.md`. **Start here — this is the cleanest evidence.**

issue.description:
Split from bf-51fq (umbrella). The observation bead (bf-51fq) cannot complete because the runtime fusion->tracker pipeline emits 0 tracked blobs even though spaxel-sim streams cleanly. This bead pins the root cause.

## Established ground truth (re-verified 2026-07-07)
- spaxel-sim streams at 240 FPS, all 4 nodes connect + get roles, fleet coverage climbs to ~21%, ZERO REJECTs/token errors. Confirmed both via blob_observation.sh and e2e TestFullE2EIntegration.
- BUT peak_blob_count=0 over a 40s run; e2e AssertDuringRun also reports "max concurrent blobs: 0, detection events: 0".
- The tracker WORKS in unit tests: tracker_test.go tr.Update([][4]float64{...}) -> 1 blob. So the defect is NOT the tracker.
- Runtime bridge (cmd/mothership/main.go ~line 2030-2064, Phase 6, 10 Hz):
    result := fusionEngine.Fuse(gatherFusionLinks(pm))
    blobs := blobTracker.track(result)
    pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)
  0 blobs => Fuse() returned 0 peaks => gatherFusionLinks(pm) handed the fusion engine nothing usable, OR Fuse's peak gate rejected it.

## Task
Pin the EXACT point where sim CSI fails to become fusion peaks. Suspects to check in order:
1. gatherFusionLinks(pm) — does it return the sim's links at all? Is a motion/variance threshold gating them out?
2. fusionEngine.Fuse() (mothership/internal/fusion/fusion.go) — peak-detection threshold / min-link-count / Fresnel geometry gate the synthetic CSI cannot cross.
3. Whether spaxel-sim's synthetic CSI actually perturbs link RSSI/motion the way the fusion gate expects (compare sim CSI shape vs what Fuse requires).

Deliverable: a comment stating the root cause (file:line + the specific gate/threshold/wiring) and the minimal change needed to make Fuse emit >=1 peak from sim CSI. No code fix yet (that is the next bead).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified with file:line evidence (where sim CSI is dropped/ignored in the fusion path).
- [ ] Minimal-fix proposal written as a comment on this bead.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-20q9o, 2026-07-07T21:21:30.439244796Z, author cli]
## ROOT CAUSE (verified at HEAD 2026-07-07): splitLinkID/gatherFusionLinks drop EVERY sim link on a delimiter mismatch — sim CSI never reaches Fuse's peak gate

**Summary:** sim CSI is dropped *before* it reaches `Fuse`. The runtime bridge calls `Fuse(gatherFusionLinks(pm))`, but `gatherFusionLinks` returns an **empty slice** because `splitLinkID` parses a delimiter (`-`) that the LinkID never contains. So `Fuse([])` -> 0 active links -> 0 peaks -> 0 blobs. The tracker is exonerated (matches tracker_test). Suspects #2 (Fuse peak/minDelta gate) and #3 (sim CSI shape) are **not even reached** by this bug — the motion/variance gate and Fresnel geometry are never evaluated.

**The chain (all verified at HEAD, not from the timed-out trace):**

1. `CSIFrame.LinkID()` — `mothership/internal/ingestion/frame.go:119-121`:
   `return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", f.MACString(), f.PeerMACString())`
   `MACString()/PeerMACString()` -> `macToString` (frame.go:124-127) = uppercase colon hex. So LinkID = `"AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11:22:33:44:55:66"` — **colon-joined, NO dash.**

2. Ingest stores it verbatim into the processor manager: `server.go:689 linkID := frame.LinkID()` -> `pm.Process(linkID,...)` keys `pm.processors[linkID]` verbatim (processor.go:254-257); `GetAllMotionStates()` returns `lp.linkID` as-is (processor.go:119). There is **no** `CanonicalLinkID` anywhere in the tree.

3. `splitLinkID` — `mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:5407-5415`: scans the string back-to-front for a `-`. The colon-joined LinkID has no `-`, so it falls through to `return nil` for **every** link.

4. `gatherFusionLinks` — `main.go:5428-5432`: `parts := splitLinkID(s.LinkID)`; `if len(parts) != 2 { continue }` -> every state skipped -> returns an empty `links` slice.

5. Runtime bridge — `main.go:2056-2058`:
   `result := fusionEngine.Fuse(gatherFusionLinks(pm))` -> `Fuse([])`.
   `blobs := blobTracker.track(result)` -> 0 blobs -> `pm.SetTrackedBlobs([])`.

6. `Fuse` — `mothership/internal/fusion/fusion.go:188`: `for _, lm := range links` over an empty slice -> `activeLinks` stays 0 -> no `grid.AddLinkInfluence` -> no peaks. (The gate at `fusion.go:189` `if !lm.Motion || lm.DeltaRMS < minDelta` is never even reached.)

**Both blob paths are broken identically:** the 2D self-improving localizer uses the same `splitLinkID` at `main.go:2786`, so it also gets 0 links.

**Why prior runs "failed" 3x:** the diagnostic spans fusion.go, gatherFusionLinks/splitLinkID, both sim generators, ingestion, and the signal pipeline (~30 file reads). Each prior run hit the 600s timeout mid-investigation (exit 124) — the prior run had actually reached this same finding but ran out of time before posting it. This run harvested that timed-out trace and verified the full chain at HEAD instead of restarting.

## MINIMAL-FIX PROPOSAL (no code change in THIS bead — the fix is the next bead)

Make the LinkID delimiter and its parser agree. Two options; recommend (B):

- **(B — recommended, matches documented intent):** `splitLinkID`'s own docstring (main.go:5408) says the format is `"aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-11:22:33:44:55:66"` (dash between the two MACs). Fix the producer to match the parser's documented contract: change `frame.go:120` from `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", ...)` to `fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", ...)`. `splitLinkID` then splits at the single `-` correctly for both the 2D (main.go:2786) and 3D (main.go:5429) paths. *Blast radius:* `LinkID()` is also the key for the `server.go` ring buffers (`s.links[linkID]`, lines 678/685/689) and recording files (`rec.Write`) — all producer<->consumer at runtime, so self-consistent; only the on-disk recording-key format changes.

- **(A — lower blast radius):** keep `LinkID()` colon-joined; fix the parser to split on the fixed MAC width (each MAC is exactly 17 chars, `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`): in `splitLinkID`, `if len(linkID) >= 35 { return []string{linkID[:17], linkID[18:]} }; return nil`. One function, fixes both paths, no key-format change — but brittle to future format tweaks.

**Verified preconditions for the fix (so the fix bead isn't chasing a phantom):** once the split is corrected, `parts[0]` = uppercase colon node MAC (`macToString` form), which matches the `nodePos` key seeded from `fleetReg` `node.MAC` (main.go:1151, sourced from the hello `mac` field in `"AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"` form per ingestion fuzz tests) -> `Fuse`'s `nodePos[lm.NodeMAC]` lookups (fusion.go:192-193) will resolve. So this single wiring fix is sufficient to get sim CSI *into* Fuse. Whether sim amplitudes then clear `minDelta` (fusion.go:189) becomes the next bead's question (suspect #3, previously masked by this upstream drop).

**Acceptance criteria — both met:**
- [x] Root cause identified with file:line evidence: `splitLinkID` (main.go:5407-5415) drops the colon-joined LinkID produced by `CSIFrame.LinkID()` (frame.go:119-121).
- [x] Minimal-fix proposal written: Option A / Option B above.

Closing as diagnosed. The code fix (and verifying sim amplitude clears `minDelta`) is the next bead.

## Objective
Decomposed from parent bf-5h1t (Populate canonical identity fields on a runtime blob). The blob-identity infrastructure exists but live blobs still have empty identity fields. This read-only step pinpoints the exact broken link so the fix (next child) is minimal and certain instead of another open-ended investigation that times out.

## Context already established (do NOT re-derive)
- The canonical identity fields live on signal.TrackedBlob (mothership/internal/signal/processor.go:600-607): PersonName, AssignedColor, IdentityResolved. Comments there and at internal/api/tracks.go:30 explicitly say they are zero today and a follow-up bead wires the BLE sidecar.
- Infrastructure already present: ble.IdentityMatcher is constructed at cmd/mothership/main.go:806-808 (CONDITIONAL). ~15 identityMatcher.GetMatch(blob.ID) copy sites exist at cmd/mothership/main.go:2083-2626 that write identity onto blobs. mothership/internal/tracker/ble_provider.go adapts it to an IdentityProvider.
- The blob-tracker builds TrackedBlob with NO identity fields at cmd/mothership/main.go:5568 (kinematics only). GetTrackedBlobs() (the source for /api/blobs at main.go:4305) is written via pm.SetTrackedBlobs (main.go:2065, 2152).
- Prerequisite bf-40hc is CLOSED and delivers scripts/run-sim-local.sh (see notes/hardware-free-runtime.md), which produces tracked blobs at /api/blobs (peak=2). The sim has a --ble flag (mothership/cmd/sim/main.go:56).

## Scope (read-only diagnosis — no code change, no run longer than the canonical ~30s sim)
Determine and document, with file:line evidence, the SINGLE broken link in the chain: matcher-active -> match-found -> written-onto-served-blob -> observable-at-/api/blobs. Specifically answer:
1. Is identityMatcher non-nil in the runtime path that feeds /api/blobs? (main.go:806-808 is conditional — what guard, and is it satisfied by scripts/run-sim-local.sh?)
2. Do the GetMatch copy sites write onto the SAME []TrackedBlob that SetTrackedBlobs/GetTrackedBlobs serves, or a different in-memory blob set?
3. Does main.go:5568 (tracker output, identity-less) feed SetTrackedBlobs and bypass the copy sites?
4. Does sim --ble actually register BLE devices into the registry the matcher reads, so GetMatch can return non-nil?

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A comment is posted on this bead naming the exact broken link(s) with file:line references and the minimal change(s) needed to make a live blob carry non-empty identity.
- [ ] OR a confirmed finding (with evidence) that identity DOES already flow under a specific runtime config — in which case state the exact config/flags so the observe child can use it directly.

The IdentityMatcher never produces a match because no BLE device is registered as a *person* in the registry. The downstream write-back and /api/blobs serving are intact. Evidence per sub-question:

**Q1 — is identityMatcher non-nil in the /api/blobs path? YES.** Guard at main.go:807 is `if bleRegistry != nil`. bleRegistry = ble.NewRegistry("$DATA_DIR/ble.db") (main.go:790-800); run-sim-local.sh uses a fresh mktemp DATA_DIR (run-sim-local.sh:74) so ble.db opens/creates fine => bleRegistry != nil => identityMatcher = ble.NewIdentityMatcher(...) (main.go:808) is non-nil. Nothing in run-sim-local.sh disables BLE. Matcher IS active in the runtime path.

**Q2 — do the GetMatch copy sites write the SAME served slice? YES (link intact).** The bf-5h1t write-back at main.go:2137-2151 mutates the same `blobs` slice in place (blobs[i].PersonName/AssignedColor/IdentityResolved = match.*; main.go:2148-2150) and re-publishes via pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs) at main.go:2152. /api/blobs reads pm.GetTrackedBlobs() at main.go:4305 — same pm.trackedBlobs field (processor.go:640-653). The identity-less output is overwritten, not bypassed — conditional on GetMatch != nil.

**Q4 — does sim --ble register a device the matcher reads, so GetMatch can return non-nil? NO — THIS IS THE BUG.**
- Matcher triangulates ONLY registered person devices: triangulateAllDevices (internal/ble/identity.go:153-159) iterates registry.GetAllPersonDevicesWithAliases() -> GetAllPersonDevices() (internal/ble/registry.go:1136) which filters `WHERE d.person_id IS NOT NULL AND d.is_archived = 0 AND d.enabled = 1`.
- sim --ble (cmd/sim/main.go:1126-1173, sendBLEMessages) emits raw advertisements for walker addr `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:%02X` (cmd/sim/main.go:1142). These reach the BLE handler (main.go:1749-1785): rssiCache.AddWithTime populates RSSI correctly (main.go:1767) AND bleRegistry.ProcessRelayMessage is called (main.go:1781).
- BUT ProcessRelayMessage (registry.go:378-417) UPSERTs ble_devices WITHOUT setting person_id — it stays NULL (a *discovered* device, not a person device). person_id is set ONLY by AssignDeviceToPerson (registry.go:747), reachable only via REST (PUT /api/ble/devices/{mac} with person_id, after CreatePerson; routes registered at main.go:3065-3067). Nothing in the sim or run-sim-local.sh does this.
- => GetAllPersonDevicesWithAliases() empty -> triangulateAllDevices returns nil -> assignBLEToBlobs assigns nothing -> GetMatch(blobID) returns nil (identity.go:609) -> write-back at main.go:2138-2150 never fires -> /api/blobs blobs carry empty identity.
- Compounding: run-sim-local.sh (line 118-123) does not even pass --ble, so in the canonical reproduce no BLE ads are emitted and the RSSI cache is also empty.

**OR-criterion (identity already flows under some config)? FALSE.** No sim/runtime config today registers a person device, so identity never flows in the hardware-free path.

**Minimal fix for the next child bead** (the write-back at main.go:2137-2152 is already correct and needs NO change):
1. Add `--ble` to the run-sim-local.sh sim invocation (run-sim-local.sh:118-123) so BLE ads flow and rssiCache populates.
2. Seed a registered person whose device addr matches a walker: CreatePerson("Alice", color) then assign walker 0's addr via `PUT /api/ble/devices/AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:00` body `{"person_id":"<id>"}` (addr is deterministic per cmd/sim/main.go:1142, walker.ID=0 -> ...:00). curl it from run-sim-local.sh after the mothership is healthy, OR add a sim flag like `--ble-register-person "Alice"` that POSTs after connect.
3. Result: matcher triangulates cached RSSI (conf>=0.1), assignBLEToBlobs matches nearest blob, GetMatch returns non-nil, and the EXISTING write-back at main.go:2138-2150 populates PersonName/AssignedColor/IdentityResolved on served blobs. First match lags BLE start by the 5s BLE cadence (cmd/sim/main.go:980) + match window.

Note for the fixer: assignBLEToBlobs needs the triangulated device position near a tracked blob (match-distance gate) and >=2 reporting nodes for usable confidence — satisfied once --ble runs across the sim's multi-node fleet.

issue.description:
Interim fix from ADR-006's alternatives -- independent of the auth work and strictly less effort. Do this now regardless of whether the public-origin path is ever taken.

SPAXEL_ADVERTISED_BASE_URL is http://10.20.23.203:8080 and the node's NVS has ms_ip=10.20.23.203. That address is k3s-agent-minisforum, where the pod happens to run because the Deployment uses hostNetwork: true. Nothing pins it there. If it reschedules, both the OTA download URL and every provisioned node's mothership address break silently -- the node just stops connecting, with no indication why.

k8s/ardenone-cluster/spaxel/deployment.yml already carries this caveat in its own hostNetwork comment ('Node IP is currently 10.20.23.203 (k3s-agent-minisforum) -- will change if this pod is ever scheduled elsewhere, since nothing pins it to that node'). It was written as a known risk and never closed.

Change: add a nodeSelector (or node affinity) pinning the Deployment to k3s-agent-minisforum, and update the comment to say the IP is now durable rather than incidental.

Consider also whether a LAN-resolvable DNS name would be better than an IP -- it would survive a deliberate move, where a nodeSelector just relocates the problem. Either is better than the status quo.

Acceptance: the pod cannot be scheduled off k3s-agent-minisforum; deleting the pod reschedules it to the same node and 10.20.23.203:8080 still answers.
issue.title: Pin the spaxel pod to a node so the LAN OTA base URL stays valid

issue.description:
ADR-008 decision 5. GATES all PKI identity work. This is a measurement with a number attached, not a formality -- a bad result is allowed to send us back to the ADR-007 symmetric design.

Why: RAM is the binding constraint for certificate-based identity, and the TLS path has NEVER actually executed on this hardware. wss:// support shipped in 0.2.19, but the deployed config uses plain ws:// on the LAN (ADR-006 decision 6), so no handshake has run alongside WiFi + NimBLE + CSI. There is no measured peak-heap figure, and mTLS RAISES it -- a client key operation plus a second chain on top of server verification.

Measured statics on the current build (for reference, these are fine):
  IRAM      97,358 B (26.9% used)
  D/IRAM    59,604 B (17.2% used), 286,252 B remaining at link
  flash     1,684,597 B of 2,031,616 B slot, 346,912 B (17%) free

Two pieces of work:

1. Enable CONFIG_SPIRAM. The chip has 2MB PSRAM sitting unused -- esptool flash-id reports "Embedded PSRAM 2MB (AP_3v3)" and sdkconfig has "# CONFIG_SPIRAM is not set". This is the single biggest lever and it is config-only. Validate it ON ITS OWN, not bundled with identity work: it changes allocator placement and DMA constraints globally.

2. Surface and record free heap. The firmware already sends free_heap_bytes in its status message (websocket.c:494) and the mothership already has a free_heap_bytes column (db/migrations.go:258) -- it is simply not exposed by any API response. Surface it, then force a real TLS connection (point a node at the 443 path) and capture the peak.

Deliverable: measured free heap at idle and at TLS handshake peak, with and without PSRAM. Then an explicit go/no-go on whether mTLS client certs fit.

If NO-GO: say so plainly and fall back to ADR-007 symmetric, which is strictly cheaper in both flash and heap. ADR-008 records that this outcome is allowed.

issue.title: Spike: enable PSRAM and measure real TLS handshake heap on hardware (go/no-go for PKI identity)

issue.description:
Find the per-test loop with index 'i' in main() and analyze how the index variable is used. Identify where -Wclobbered might trigger based on setjmp/longjmp patterns or other control flow that could clobber the loop variable.

This is child 3/3 of spaxel-2e6ac585 split.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identified the specific per-test loop with index 'i'
- Analyzed how 'i' is used within the loop body
- Predicted where -Wclobbered might trigger based on the code structure
- Documented the specific code patterns that could cause clobbering
issue.notes:
Premise-false / already-landed — verify-only close, no file changes, no commit.

DELIVERABLE ALREADY AT HEAD: the per-test loop and its full -Wclobbered analysis exist in-tree, committed in bf-era commits 85cd76db (volatile-qualify the loop index for a -Wclobbered-clean build) and a552e059 (the C11 7.13.2.1 clobber-audit comment at the setjmp call site). Verified against HEAD itself via git grep 'CLOBBER AUDIT' HEAD -- firmware/test/test_runner.c — not working-tree-only (git status is clean under firmware/test/).

All 4 ACs answered by firmware/test/test_runner.c:
1. LOOP IDENTIFIED: main() at line 225, per-test loop at line 236 — for (volatile int i = 0; i < g_test_count; i++). This is the repo's ONLY setjmp site (grep setjmp/longjmp across firmware/ hits test_runner.c and test_runner.h only).
2. i USAGE: written ONLY by the for-init (i=0) and the for-increment (i++); the loop body only READS it (g_tests[i].name in the RUN printf, g_tests[i].fn() call). The increment runs after control resumes at the setjmp call site, so no write to i lands between the setjmp() call and a longjmp fired inside g_tests[i].fn() — C11 7.13.2.1's changed-between-setjmp-and-longjmp condition is not met, so i is determinate on the longjmp-return path where i++ and the i < g_test_count re-test consume it.
3. WHERE -Wclobbered TRIGGERS (predicted by the in-file audit at lines 305-338; independently re-verified live today on gcc 15.2.0 — the comment recorded gcc 14, so this is a newer-compiler confirmation, not a stale claim):
   - Baseline as committed (volatile i + preceding qsort): SILENT at -O0/-O1/-O2/-Os with explicit -Wclobbered, rc=0, no output.
   - Control A — volatile stripped, qsort call KEPT: still SILENT at all four levels, confirming the audit's claim that the incidental qsort call keeps gcc's register heuristic quiet.
   - Control B — volatile stripped AND the qsort call removed: -Wclobbered FIRES on i at -O1, -O2 and -Os ('variable i might be clobbered by longjmp or vfork', pointing at the for-statement); -O0 stays silent because the warning comes out of an optimization pass. Exactly the audit's 'warns at -O1..-Os' prediction.
   - The CI gate (-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -O2) is therefore clean as committed; the volatile on i is load-bearing, not cargo cult — strip it and the real gate goes red the moment the qsort stops biasing the heuristic.
4. CLOBBER PATTERNS DOCUMENTED: (a) an automatic loop index local to main() spanning a setjmp/longjmp boundary inside the same function — the exact shape gcc's heuristic flags; (b) the body call is gated on if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) with NO else, so a failed assertion falls through to i++ with the index intact (failure in test N never blocks N+1..end); (c) the longjmp originates in a DIFFERENT function (test_record_failure), so no automatic object in main() is written between the setjmp and the longjmp; (d) the run-wide state (g_failure_count, g_test_jmp) is file-scope static, which 7.13.2.1 does not reach at all, and main() holds no local tallies — hence i is the only clobber candidate in the frame, and volatile exempts it from both the indeterminate rule and the warning with zero behavior change.

Method: negative controls compiled from /tmp copies with -I firmware/test, objects written to /tmp — no repo file touched. Sibling blocker spaxel-8aac8ede (child 2/3 of the same split) closed 2026-09-04 with the same loop location plus a live make -C firmware/test test run (60 tests, all green); its stale-embedded-counts side finding (line 247-304 comment still says 29 tests vs today's 60) stands and is not re-litigated here. Declining a split: nothing to split — the unit of work is complete and published. split-child label retained (structural).

issue.description:
mothership/internal/explainability/handler.go refreshData() (POST /api/explain/refresh handler, ~line 323-341), Component 28 Detection Explainability (docs/plan/plan.md ~line 2021-2043), sets the stored fusion result snapshot timestamp like this:

    h.fusionResult = &FusionResultSnapshot{
        Timestamp: int64(req.GridData.Rows), // placeholder
        Blobs:     req.Blobs,
        GridData:  req.GridData,
    }

req.GridData.Rows is the accumulation grid's row COUNT (a small integer, e.g. tens to low hundreds -- a dimension, not a time), not a Unix timestamp. Whatever consumes FusionResultSnapshot.Timestamp downstream (staleness checks, "why is this here" explanation ordering/display, any freshness comparison against real wall-clock time) receives a value that resolves to a date near the Unix epoch (1970) rather than the actual refresh time -- silently wrong, not merely imprecise.

No open or in-progress bead currently tracks this specific line (distinct from the GDOP-improvement placeholder bf-68vvo and the other in-progress placeholder beads already filed -- checked title/description text of all open+in-progress beads, none reference GridData.Rows or this handler).

Fix: replace with an actual timestamp -- time.Now().UnixMilli() (matching the Unix-milliseconds convention used elsewhere in this plan/codebase, e.g. the WebSocket JSON message schemas' timestamp_ms fields) at the point refreshData receives the POST, unless the caller (dashboard) is expected to supply its own capture timestamp in the request body, in which case add a Timestamp field to the request struct and thread it through instead of fabricating one. Check how FusionResultSnapshot.Timestamp is actually consumed (grep explainability package + dashboard/js callers of /api/explain) to pick the correct one. Add/adjust a unit test in mothership/internal/explainability asserting the stored Timestamp is a plausible current-time value (e.g. within a few seconds of time.Now()), not derived from grid dimensions. Verify with: cd mothership && go test ./internal/explainability/... -v.
issue.title: Explainability refreshData sets Timestamp from GridData.Rows instead of an actual time (meaningless value)

issue.description:
Umbrella for defects found during the **first on-hardware validation of firmware/** (2026-07-28). Until this date the ESP32-S3 firmware had never been compiled or run against real hardware: CI (`spaxel-build`) only builds the mothership Docker image, and `docs/notes/firmware-host-test-approach.md` records that ESP-IDF was not even installed on the host that made the host-test decision. All PROGRESS.md validation to date is simulator-driven (`cmd/sim`), which by construction cannot exercise `firmware/main/*`.

What was verified on hardware:
- Target board: ESP32-S3 (QFN56) rev v0.2, 4 MB embedded flash + 2 MB PSRAM, native USB-Serial/JTAG only (USB ID 303a:1001), no USB-UART bridge present.
- `firmware/` compiles clean under ESP-IDF v5.2 (5 cosmetic warnings only). App binary 1,631,552 bytes — fits the 0x1F0000 factory partition with ~20% free.
- The firmware **boots and runs**: NVS schema migration, MAC read, config load, provisioning window, WiFi init, mDNS (`spaxel-node.local`), LED init, BLE init + scan, captive portal AP `spaxel-3DC8` with DHCP on 192.168.4.1. No panic, no boot loop.

So the firmware is far healthier than "never compiled" would suggest — but three functional defects were exposed that no simulator run could have caught, plus the process gap that let them sit unnoticed. Children of this bead cover each.

Closes when all children are closed and a node has been observed streaming CSI frames to a live mothership.

issue.notes:
Documentation delivered in docs/notes/dashboard-mothership-integration.md (commit 7cbc90f6, pushed to origin/main via merge 3464bae8).

Acceptance criteria, each verified against live code:
1. go:embed — exactly ONE directive for the dashboard, in mothership/cmd/mothership/dashboard_embed.go behind a //go:build embed tag: //go:embed dashboard -> embeddedDashboardFS, with init() setting dashboardFS/dashboardEmbedded. main.go:80/:84 hold the zero-value vars for non-embed builds. Dockerfile:44-46 copies repo-root dashboard/ into cmd/mothership/dashboard/ before the build; Dockerfile:52 passes -tags=embed. The staging dir is intentionally untracked (untagged local builds fall back to the filesystem). Served via fs.Sub + http.FileServer on r.Get("/*") AND r.Head("/*") (HEAD added per bf-1cgqe); named routes /ambient /fleet /live /setup /simple go through serveEmbeddedFile(); "/" has no explicit route — it falls out of the catch-all. Fallback resolver findDashboardDir() tries cfg.StaticDir, ./dashboard, ./../dashboard, /app/dashboard, then an executable-relative upward walk. Guard test: cmd/mothership/dashboard_static_test.go.
2. WebSocket endpoints — GET /ws/dashboard (main.go:4896 -> internal/dashboard/server.go:63) and GET /ws/node (main.go:783 -> internal/ingestion/server.go:528, node-only). /ws/dashboard protocol: first frame is always {"type":"snapshot",...} built by Hub.buildSnapshot (hub.go:655) and sent BEFORE the client joins the broadcast map (ordering guarantee, hub.go:361-383); then 100 ms delta frames from tickDelta (hub.go:750) that omit "type" and carry only fields whose JSON changed vs the snapshotCache; plus 60 s system-health, 5 s BLE-scan tickers and typed event pushes (node_connected/disconnected, link_active/inactive, blob_explain {"type":"blob_explain","blob_id":N,"snapshot":{...}} at hub.go:252, zone/portal changes, self-heal coverage before/after). Client->server commands in handleCommand (server.go:126+): replay_seek, replay_play, replay_pause, replay_set_params, replay_apply_to_live. Keepalive 30 s ping / 60 s read deadline. gorilla upgrader allows all origins, per-client send buffer 1024. Five independent frontend connect sites: js/websocket.js:134 (main), home-cards.js:260, simple-mode.js:16, onboard.js:1399, ambient.js:295.
3. REST API — 181 distinct route patterns: 92 in cmd/mothership/main.go plus internal/api/ (simulator 22, localization 17, prediction 12, replay 11, zones 10, volume_triggers 10, briefing 9, guided 8, triggers/security/notifications/alerts/settings variants 3-5 each). Families the dashboard JS actually calls are enumerated in the doc.
4. Related components — mothership/ (55 internal/ packages), firmware/ ESP-IDF C (talks /ws/node only; dashboard touches it via Web Serial onboarding: esptool-bundle.js + /api/provision + /firmware/serial/{filename}), cmd/sim (spaxel-sim), test/acceptance + mothership/test/acceptance, go.work stitching all three modules. dashboard/ is vanilla JS + Three.js, 85 js/ files, 9 HTML entry points, service worker + PWA manifest.

Finding worth a follow-up (not fixed here, out of scope for a docs bead): the PIN auth flow exists (/api/auth/status|install-secret|setup|login|logout|change-pin, sessions table, spaxel_session cookie) but RequireAuth is wired to only TWO routes — /api/auth/change-pin (handler.go:188,200) and /api/doctor (main.go:5053). Nothing in internal/api/ references it, and HandleDashboardWS upgrades without consulting the session cookie. plan.md states session-cookie auth on all /api/* and on the dashboard WS upgrade; the code does not enforce that boundary today.

Verification: cd mothership && go vet ./... -> exit 0. go build ./... -> ok. go test ./... -> every package passed EXCEPT github.com/spaxel/mothership/tests/e2e, which failed on "listen tcp 127.0.0.1:8080: bind: address already in use" before any assertion ran. issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 3. Sizing work first -- this may not fit.

Two separate things:

1. Flash encryption (CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED, currently not set). Makes an NVS dump useless. Most valuable during phase 1 while the per-device key still lives in NVS, but it is an irreversible eFuse burn, so it trades one risk for another. Consider also CONFIG_SECURE_ROM_DL_MODE_ENABLED, currently y -- disabling or restricting ROM download mode closes the esptool read path that was used to extract the credential on 2026-08-07, at the cost of making recovery harder on a rig where recovery is already unreliable (bf-4z6wh).

2. Secure Boot v2 (CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT, currently not set; CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2_RSA_SUPPORTED=y and CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2_PREFERRED=y so the hardware is willing). This is what closes the HMAC_UP oracle limitation from phase 2 -- without it, hostile firmware on the device can ask the peripheral to sign anything.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS BOOTLOADER SIZE. docs/notes/esp32-ota-and-reconnection-handoff.md measured only ~11,056 bytes free in the bootloader, and Secure Boot v2 signature verification is not free. Measure before promising this: the current build reports Bootloader binary size 0x51b0 with 0x2e50 (36%) free, so the headroom is real but tight.

Start with a sizing spike and a written go/no-go, not an implementation. If it does not fit, the honest outcome is that phase 2 proves THIS CHIP but not WHICH FIRMWARE, and that limitation is documented in ADR-007 rather than quietly assumed away.

Acceptance: a measured report of bootloader size with Secure Boot v2 enabled, a go/no-go, and if go, a staged rollout plan that accounts for the burns being irreversible.
issue.title: Phase 3: size and enable flash encryption + Secure Boot v2

issue.description:
Split from bf-2eub9 (umbrella). CHILD 1 of the bf-2eub9 chain. Apply the root-cause fix pinned by bf-20q9o (closed) so spaxel-sim's CSI stops being dropped before it reaches Fuse.

## Root cause (from bf-20q9o)
CSIFrame.LinkID() (mothership/internal/ingestion/frame.go:119-121) joins the two MACs with ':' -> "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11:22:33:44:55:66" (colon-joined, NO dash). splitLinkID (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:5421) scanned only for '-' and returned nil for every link, so gatherFusionLinks returned an empty slice -> Fuse([]) -> 0 peaks -> 0 blobs. Both blob paths are broken identically (2D localizer at main.go:2786 uses the same splitLinkID).

## Task
Land the splitLinkID fix already drafted in the working tree: a fixed-width split (each MAC is exactly 17 chars "XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX"; canonical two-MAC form is 35 chars with the boundary at index 17) that handles BOTH the actual colon-joined producer format AND the documented dash format, keeping the '-' scan as a defensive fallback. This is Option A from bf-20q9o (one function, fixes both paths, no key-format change). Commit it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] splitLinkID returns [nodeMAC, peerMAC] for the colon-joined LinkID the producer actually emits (verified by a quick unit assertion or debug print).
- [ ] With spaxel-sim streaming, gatherFusionLinks(pm) returns >=1 link (Fuse receives a non-empty links slice) — confirm via the FUSE-DBG log added in fusion.go showing links>=1.
- [ ] Both blob paths use the corrected split (3D gatherFusionLinks at main.go:5446 AND 2D localizer at main.go:2786).
- [ ] Change committed.

[migrated comment from bf-561zr, 2026-07-07T22:31:34.365970161Z, author cli]
Landed splitLinkID fixed-width split (bf-561zr, commit b9f362c, pushed to origin main).

Root cause (bf-20q9o): CSIFrame.LinkID() joins the two MACs with ':' -> 'AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:11:22:33:44:55:66' (35 chars, boundary at index 17). splitLinkID scanned only for '-' and returned nil for every such link. Both fusion paths share splitLinkID (3D gatherFusionLinks main.go:5446 + 2D selfImprovingLocalizer main.go:2786), so gatherFusionLinks returned [] -> Fuse([]) -> 0 peaks -> 0 blobs.

Fix (Option A, one function, both paths, no key-format change): fixed-width split — len==35 -> split at index 17, handles both ':' (producer) and '-' (documented) separators. '-' scan kept as defensive fallback.

Acceptance:
- [x] splitLinkID returns [nodeMAC, peerMAC] for colon-joined producer LinkID — verified by TestSplitLinkID (6 table cases incl. upper/lower colon + dash) + TestSplitLinkIDProducerContract. Old code returned nil; new returns the two MACs.
