**VERDICT: (b) — the WS feed carries NO blobs. The defect is mothership EMISSION, not downstream render/probe.**

### Runtime evidence
Capture tool: `docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/capture-ws-frames.mjs` (v3, binary-vs-text aware, direct ws client on SIM_PORT 8088, 12 s window). Full output: `identity-less.ws-frames.json`.

- 4368 binary frames (raw CSI via BroadcastCSI) + 241 JSON text frames captured
- **0 / 241** JSON text frames carry a `blobs` array — including the very first `snapshot` frame and all 120 `<no-type>` delta ticks (10 Hz × 12 s)
- type histogram (text): `{snapshot:1, event:98, <no-type>:120, motion_state:22}`
- `blob_field_census: {}` (no frame anywhere has a top-level `blobs` key)
- At the same instant, `/api/blobs` returns **2 blobs** with positions/ids (api_peak_blob_count=2; 8/24 api samples had blobs)

### Sample frame excerpt (snapshot — the first message on connect)
The snapshot carries `links`, `motion_states` (several motion_detected:true, delta_rms up to ~6.5), `nodes` (4 sim nodes), `zones:[]`, `timestamp_ms`, `type:"snapshot"` — and **no `blobs` field at all**:
```
{"links":[...12...],"motion_states":[{...,"motion_detected":true,"delta_rms":6.55...},...],
 "nodes":[4 sim ESP32-S3],"timestamp_ms":1785048619486,"type":"snapshot","zones":[]}
```
Compare `/api/blobs` at t=1785048619488 (same instant):
```
[{"ID":1,"X":4.7,"Y":0.3,"Z":1.9,"VX":0,"Weight":0.82,"identityResolved":false}, ...count:2]
```
The console "detection events by blob #N" flood is real — those are the 98 `event` frames emitted by `eventsHandler.LogEvent("detection",...)` in the tracker goroutine. They carry blob_id in `event.detail_json` but are not blob render data.

### Root cause (code-level, deterministic)
`Hub.BroadcastLocUpdate(blobs)` — `internal/dashboard/hub.go:566` — is the **sole writer** of `h.snap.blobsJSON`, which both `buildSnapshot()` (hub.go:797) and `tickDelta()` (hub.go:688) read to populate the `blobs` field/key. **`BroadcastLocUpdate` has ZERO callers in the entire codebase** (`grep -rn '.BroadcastLocUpdate('` → empty).

The live tracker goroutine (`cmd/mothership/main.go` ~2110-2200, 10 Hz) does:
1. `fusionEngine.Fuse(...)` → peaks
2. `blobTracker.track(result)` → blobs
3. `pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)` ← ONLY publish path → feeds `/api/blobs` + `/api/tracks` (why those return 2 blobs)
4. `eventsHandler.LogEvent("detection",...)` ← the console flood
5. identity matcher update + write-back

It never bridges blobs into the dashboard hub. The `BlobBroadcaster` interface that `BroadcastLocUpdate` satisfies is wired **only** to the replay handler (`replayHandler.SetBlobBroadcaster(dashboardHub)`, main.go:1784), never the live tracker.

Net: `/api/blobs` independently returns live blobs; `/ws/dashboard` snapshot+delta both read an eternally-empty `blobsJSON`. Downstream render/probe code is exonerated — there is nothing on the wire for it to render.

### Fix location (for the fix bead, not this one)
In the tracker goroutine after `pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)`, add `dashboardHub.BroadcastLocUpdate(toTrackingBlobs(blobs))` (the hub expects `[]tracking.Blob`; TrackedBlob → tracking.Blob conversion needed), guarded by `dashboardHub != nil`. No code change made in this diagnosis-only bead.

issue.description:
Second link of the bf-4iewr split (depends on the root-cause finding). The token the sim provisions never reaches the validator — make the token path REAL so a sim node presenting a valid token is accepted even when the migration window is closed.

## Problem (confirmed by the root-cause child)
- Validator reads only `hello.Token` (`internal/ingestion/server.go:513`).
- Sim sends its token only as the `X-Spaxel-Token` HTTP header (`cmd/sim/main.go:633`), never in the hello body, and the mothership never reads that header. So `hello.Token` is always "" and every node falls through to the migration-window branch.

## Scope
Pick ONE bridging approach and implement it (justify the choice in the PR/comment):
- (A) Server-side: in the `/ws/node` upgrade handler, read `X-Spaxel-Token` from the WS handshake request and inject it into the parsed hello (`nc.Hello.Token` / the value passed to the validator) before the validation check at server.go:506-530; OR
- (B) Client-side: have the sim include a `"token"` field in the hello JSON body (`cmd/sim/main.go` hello map ~640, and `cmd/sim/scenario.go`).

Prefer the option that keeps real ESP32 firmware behavior unchanged (firmware today sends token in hello — verify against `firmware/main/websocket.c`). Do not weaken the validator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A node presenting a VALID provisioned token is accepted and marked paired (not Unpaired) even when `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (window closed) — proven by a test.
- [ ] A node presenting an INVALID/empty token is still REJECTED when the window is closed (regression guard; do not break rejection).
- [ ] Test (unit or e2e) exercises the bridge end-to-end through `ValidateToken` (`internal/provisioning/server.go:135`, HMAC-SHA256(installSecret, mac)).

issue.description:
Root-caused the 'post-reflash silence' / 'device did not become ready after
flashing' failure that blocked ESP32-S3 onboarding, via direct serial/USB
debugging on bench (dozens of BOOT/RST/power-cycle cycles, usbmon capture).
Three compounding issues, all fixed:

1. firmware/main/provision.c listened on physical UART0 (GPIO43/44) for the
   provisioning handshake, but this board has no USB-UART bridge chip --
   only native USB-Serial-JTAG. Boot logs worked (console correctly routed
   per sdkconfig.defaults), but the provisioning listener's UART0 traffic
   went nowhere. Fixed: switched to the usb_serial_jtag driver (same
   peripheral console/esp_log already uses), following the install pattern
   from ESP-IDF's own esp_console_repl.c.

2. Dockerfile's firmware merge_bin step wrote the app to 0x10000, which was
   correct under the OLD partition table but became the `otadata` partition
   after the 2026-07-30 true-A/B migration (ADR-004/bf-436bh) moved app
   slots to 0x20000/0x210000. Every wizard reflash was silently corrupting
   otadata (and the start of ota_0) while the bootloader kept booting
   whatever old image happened to already be in an OTA slot -- explains why
   reflashing never seemed to change behavior. Fixed: merge now includes
   ota_data_initial.bin at 0x10000 and places the app at 0x20000, matching
   `idf.py build`'s own suggested flash-args for the current partitions.csv.

3. Even with both fixes, the native USB-Serial-JTAG RX path is intermittently
   unreliable at the USB level -- confirmed via usbmon that a bulk OUT
   transfer can be submitted by the host and never acknowledged by the
   device, while the SAME device's TX (SPAXEL READY broadcasts, esp_log) is
   100% reliable every time. This looks like an ESP32-S3 silicon/driver
   errata, not an application bug -- the ESP-IDF usb_serial_jtag driver's
   install/ISR code was reviewed and matches the reference implementation.
   Mitigated rather than fixed: dashboard/js/onboard.js now (a) retries the
   provisioning JSON write up to 5x, and (b) no longer treats a missing
   serial ack as fatal -- only an explicit {"ok":false,...} response is.
   Real confirmation of success now comes from the existing detect_node step
   polling /api/nodes for the node to appear online over WiFi, which is
   strictly stronger proof than a serial ack (the device can only do that
   with working credentials actually written to NVS).

Verified end-to-end on bench: fixed firmware boots today's build (not a
stale cached image), broadcasts SPAXEL READY reliably, and a clean
single-shot write after a full power-cycle succeeds at the USB level.
issue.title: Onboarding wizard 'device did not become ready' -- root-caused to 3 compounding bugs, fixed

## Task
Read and catalog all GDOP-related functions from mothership/internal/simulator/gdop.go

## Scope
Focus on mothership/internal/simulator/gdop.go specifically:
- GDOPComputer struct
- ComputeAt method
- ComputeAll method
- Any other GDOP-related functions

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Read the file mothership/internal/simulator/gdop.go
- [ ] List all public GDOP-related functions with their full signatures

- [ ] Note parameter types and return types for each function

## Deliverable
Updated notes in this bead with catalog of gdop.go functions complete.
issue.notes:
GDOP catalog complete:

## Structs

### GDOPComputer
- links: []Link — TX→RX communication pairs for coverage analysis
- config: GridConfig — Spatial grid configuration (cell size, bounds)
- maxZone: int — Maximum Fresnel zone to consider (default: 3)

### GDOPResult
- X, Y, Z: float64 — Cell center position (meters)
- GDOP: float64 — Computed GDOP value (Infinity = no coverage)
- Quality: string — "excellent"/"good"/"fair"/"poor"/"none"
- ContributingLinks: []string — Link IDs covering this cell ("TX_ID:RX_ID")

### GridConfig
- CellSize: float64 — Grid cell size in meters (default: 0.2m)
- MinX, MinY: float64 — Grid origin coordinates
- Width: float64 — Grid width (X dimension)
- Depth: float64 — Grid depth (Y dimension)

### GDOPHeatmapData
- Width, Depth: int — Grid dimensions
- CellSize: float64 — Cell size in meters
- OriginX, OriginY: float64 — Grid origin
- GDOPValues: []float64 — Flattened GDOP values (9999 = infinity)
- Qualities: []string — Flattened quality strings
- Colors: [][]uint8 — Flattened RGB colors [width*depth*3]
- AccuracyMap: []float64 — Expected accuracy per cell (meters)

### GDOPColor
- R, G, B: uint8 — RGB values 0-255

## Public Functions (exported)

### Constructor
- NewGDOPComputer(links []Link, config GridConfig) *GDOPComputer
  — Creates GDOP computer with grid config, defaults CellSize to 0.2m, maxZone to 3

### Configuration
- (gc *GDOPComputer) SetMaxZone(zone int)
  — Sets maximum Fresnel zone to consider (minimum 1)

### Computation
- (gc *GDOPComputer) ComputeAll() [][]GDOPResult
  — Returns 2D array [row][col] of GDOP results for entire grid
  — Z fixed at 1.0m for 2D analysis

- (gc *GDOPComputer) ComputeAt(x, y, z float64) GDOPResult
  — Computes GDOP at specific 3D point
  — Returns GDOP, quality, and contributing links
  — Quality thresholds: excellent (<2), good (2-4), fair (4-8), poor (>8), none (∞)

### Analysis
- (gc *GDOPComputer) CoverageScore(results [][]GDOPResult) float64
  — Returns percentage of cells with "excellent" or "good" coverage

- (gc *GDOPComputer) AverageGDOP(results [][]GDOPResult) float64
  — Returns average GDOP across all cells (excludes infinity)

- (gc *GDOPComputer) QualityCounts(results [][]GDOPResult) map[string]int
  — Returns count of cells by quality level

- (gc *GDOPComputer) FindDeadZones(results [][]GDOPResult) []Point
  — Returns positions where quality is "none" or "poor"

- (gc *GDOPComputer) RecommendNodePosition(results [][]GDOPResult, space *Space) Point
  — Suggests optimal position for additional node (centroid of dead zones or space center)

- (gc *GDOPComputer) GetWorstCoverageCells(results [][]GDOPResult, n int) []GDOPResult
  — Returns N cells with worst GDOP values (descending sort)

- (gc *GDOPComputer) GetBestCoverageCells(results [][]GDOPResult, n int) []GDOPResult
  — Returns N cells with best GDOP values (ascending sort)

### Visualization
- (gc *GDOPComputer) ToHeatmapData(results [][]GDOPResult) *GDOPHeatmapData
  — Converts results to flattened heatmap format for frontend rendering

- (gc *GDOPComputer) ComputeAccuracyMap(results [][]GDOPResult) [][]float64
  — Returns 2D array of expected accuracy values per cell (meters, ∞ = no coverage)

- (gc *GDOPComputer) ComputeColorMap(results [][]GDOPResult) [][]uint8
  — Returns flattened RGB color array [width*depth*3]

### Optimization
- OptimizeNodePositions(space *Space, numNodes int, iterations int) *NodeSet
  — Greedy algorithm to find better node positions (starts with corners, iterates N times)

- GenerateShoppingList(space *Space, currentNodes *NodeSet) *ShoppingList
  — Creates shopping list with min nodes, recommended count, expected accuracy, coverage %

### Utility
- MinimumNodeCount(space *Space, targetGDOP float64) int
  — Estimates minimum nodes needed based on area and target GDOP
  — Heuristic: 15 m²/node (excellent), 20 m²/node (good), 30 m²/node (fair)

- ExpectedAccuracy(gdop float64) float64
  — Estimates localization accuracy: 0.5m × GDOP value
  — Returns ∞ if GDOP is ∞

- GDOPColorMap(gdop float64) GDOPColor
  — Returns RGB color for GDOP visualization
  — Green (excellent), Yellow (good), Orange (fair), Red (poor), Gray (none)

## Private Functions (internal)

- (gc *GDOPComputer) computeGDOPAngular(point Point, links []Link) float64
  — Core GDOP computation via 2D Fisher Information Matrix
  — Returns ∞ for < 2 links or collinear geometry

- gdopToQuality(gdop float64) string
  — Converts GDOP value to quality string

- computeGDOPImprovement(currentLayout []*Node, nodeMAC string, targetPos Point) float64
  — Computes relative improvement [-1, 1] for hypothetical node repositioning

- computeWorstGDOP(nodes []*Node) float64
  — Calculates worst-case GDOP across entire grid for a node layout

- extractNodePositions(nodes *NodeSet) []Point
  — Helper to extract positions from NodeSet

## Quality Thresholds (from gdopToQuality)
- GDOP < 2.0 → "excellent"
- 2.0 ≤ GDOP < 4.0 → "good"
- 4.0 ≤ GDOP < 8.0 → "fair"
- 8.0 ≤ GDOP < ∞ → "poor"
- GDOP = ∞ → "none"

## Color Map (GDOPColorMap)
- Excellent: RGB(34, 197, 94) — Green #22c65e
- Good: RGB(255, 193, 7) — Yellow #ffc107
- Fair: RGB(255, 146, 0) — Orange #ff9200
- Poor: RGB(220, 53, 69) — Red #dc3545
- None: RGB(80, 80, 80) — Gray

All functions documented with parameters, return types, and constraints.
issue.title: Read and catalog GDOP functions from gdop.go

issue.description:
## Background

Every detection algorithm produces errors. False positives (detected presence when no one is there) are annoying and erode trust. False negatives (missed detection of a real person) are dangerous for safety applications. The feedback loop gives users a direct mechanism to correct errors and the system learns from those corrections. Showing users measurable improvement over time ("You've provided 47 corrections. Accuracy improved 12% this week") creates a virtuous engagement loop and transforms users into active participants in improving the system.

## Feedback UI Elements

Every detection event exposed to the user should have feedback affordances. Three contexts:

1. Dashboard 3D view: Each active track has a small thumbs-up/down icon that appears on hover/focus. Clicking thumbs-down opens a quick inline form.

2. Activity timeline (Phase 8): Every detection event entry has thumbs-up/thumbs-down at the end of the row. Space-efficient: 2 icon buttons.

3. Push notifications: Fall and anomaly notifications include a quick-reply option (via ntfy actions or Pushover callbacks): "False alarm — clear this."

4. "I was here and wasn't detected" button: On the timeline panel, a button "Report missed detection" opens a form: "When? [time picker, default: now]", "Where? [zone picker]", "Who? [person picker, optional]". Submits as a FALSE_NEGATIVE feedback event with the user-provided position.

Feedback form for thumbs-down:
- "What was wrong?" (radio buttons):
  - "No one was there (false alarm)"
  - "Someone was missed at this location"
  - "Wrong person identified"
  - "Wrong zone/location"
- Optional free-text "Notes" field
- Submit / Cancel

## Feedback Storage

SQLite schema:
CREATE TABLE detection_feedback (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  event_id TEXT,          -- references events table (activity timeline)
  event_type TEXT,        -- "blob_detection", "zone_transition", "fall_alert", "anomaly"
  feedback_type TEXT,     -- "TRUE_POSITIVE", "FALSE_POSITIVE", "FALSE_NEGATIVE", "WRONG_IDENTITY", "WRONG_ZONE"
  details_json TEXT,      -- {"zone_id":"...", "person_id":"...", "notes":"..."}
  timestamp DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  applied BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,   -- set to TRUE after weight refinement processes it
  processed_at DATETIME
);

The applied flag enables incremental processing: the weight learner (Phase 7 self-improving localisation) queries WHERE applied = FALSE, processes batches, and marks them TRUE.

## Accuracy Metrics

Compute precision/recall/F1 per link, per zone, and per person weekly. This requires knowing the true positives, false positives, and false negatives.

Ground truth sources:
- User thumbs-up -> TRUE_POSITIVE for the corresponding detection event
- User thumbs-down (false alarm) -> FALSE_POSITIVE for the detection event
- User "missed detection" report -> FALSE_NEGATIVE for the reported time/zone

Note: ground truth is sparse — users will not feedback every event. We use the feedback we have as a sample. Assume events without feedback are TRUE_POSITIVE for the purpose of precision estimates (conservative: this means precision is an upper bound, not exact).

Metrics computed weekly:
- precision = TP / (TP + FP) — of all detections, what fraction were correct
- recall = TP / (TP + FN) — of all true presence events, what fraction were detected
- F1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
- Per-link metrics: which links have the most false positives (worst precision)
- Per-zone metrics: which zones are most often missed (worst recall)

Storage: detection_accuracy (week TEXT, scope_type TEXT, scope_id TEXT, precision REAL, recall REAL, f1 REAL, tp_count INT, fp_count INT, fn_count INT, computed_at DATETIME). Scope types: "system", "link", "zone", "person".

## Accuracy Trend Display

Dashboard "Accuracy" panel (in expert mode):
- Overall accuracy gauge: composite F1 score as a circular gauge (0-100%)
- Week-over-week trend graph: sparkline of weekly F1 over the last 8 weeks
- "You've provided N corrections. Your accuracy improved X% this week." — motivational counter
- Per-zone breakdown: bar chart of precision/recall per zone (click a zone bar to jump to it in 3D view)
- Per-link breakdown: link health vs. feedback score correlation (are high-health links also high-accuracy?)
- Feedback count: total corrections given, open corrections (not yet processed), processed corrections

The accuracy trend display intentionally shows the improvement trajectory, not just the absolute value, to reinforce that feedback has an effect.

## Feedback Application

Processing happens in a background goroutine (mothership/internal/learning/feedback_processor.go) that runs every 6 hours or when triggered manually.

For FALSE_POSITIVE events with associated CSI data (in the recording buffer from Phase 2):
- Retrieve the CSI data from the recording buffer at the event timestamp for all links
- Add the CSI frame data to a "known false positive" set in SQLite: false_positive_frames (link_id, timestamp, delta_rms, context_json)
- The weight learner (self-improving localisation bead) uses this set as negative examples

For FALSE_NEGATIVE events with user-reported position:
- Add to "known false negative" set: false_negative_frames (link_id, timestamp, expected_position_xyz, context_json)
- The weight learner uses this as a positive example at the specified position

After processing, mark feedback.applied = TRUE.

## Files to Create or Modify

- mothership/internal/learning/feedback_processor.go: feedback processing pipeline
- mothership/internal/analytics/accuracy.go: weekly metric computation
- dashboard/js/feedback.js: thumbs-up/down UI components (reusable across 3D view and timeline)
- dashboard/js/accuracy.js: Accuracy panel rendering
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: POST /api/feedback, GET /api/accuracy

## Tests

- Test feedback storage: POST /api/feedback with each feedback_type, verify SQLite record created
- Test accuracy metric computation with synthetic TP/FP/FN data: 8 TP, 2 FP, 1 FN -> precision=0.8, recall=0.888
- Test weekly rollup: 7 days of daily feedback -> correctly aggregated weekly metric
- Test that applied=false events are found and marked as applied after processor run
- Test "improvements" counter: feedback_count increases on each POST /api/feedback call

## Acceptance Criteria

- Thumbs-up/down buttons appear on active tracks in 3D view and on all timeline events
- "Missed detection" button and form available in timeline panel
- Feedback stored in SQLite with correct feedback_type and details
- Accuracy metrics computed weekly and stored in detection_accuracy table
- Accuracy panel shows week-over-week trend (requires at least 2 weeks of data)
- Feedback improvement counter shows correct counts
- Applied flag correctly set after processor run
- Tests pass
issue.title: Detection feedback loop and accuracy tracking

issue.description:
`firmware/CMakeLists.txt:8-14` tries to derive the firmware version from git:

    execute_process(
        COMMAND git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null
        ...
        ERROR_QUIET
    )

CMake's `execute_process(COMMAND ...)` does **not** run its argument list through a shell, so `2>/dev/null` is passed to `git` as a literal positional argument rather than being interpreted as a redirection. `git describe --tags --dirty 2>/dev/null` therefore treats it as a revision name, fails ("fatal: ambiguous argument"), and `ERROR_QUIET` hides the failure. `GIT_VERSION` comes back empty and the build silently falls through to the hardcoded fallback:

    set(PROJECT_VERSION "0.1.0")

So the firmware version never reflects the actual git tag — every build claims the fallback regardless of repo state, and the `--dirty` marker never appears. The build-time `message(STATUS "Building SPAXEL firmware version: ...")` reports the fallback too, so the log looks plausible and the bug is easy to miss. Note the repo's own `VERSION` file is at 0.1.357, so the mismatch against the fallback is large.

This matters beyond cosmetics: the version is compiled into the app descriptor and reported by nodes to the mothership, so OTA/fleet views cannot distinguish firmware builds.

Scope:
- Drop the `2>/dev/null` argument — `ERROR_QUIET` already suppresses stderr, which is what the redirect was trying to do.
- Add `RESULT_VARIABLE` and only accept `GIT_VERSION` when the command actually succeeded, rather than inferring success from a non-empty string.
- Decide whether the version should come from git at all or from the repo's `VERSION` file (0.1.357), which is what the mothership image is tagged from — consistency between the two is probably what is actually wanted. Document the choice.
- Keep a sane fallback for source builds with no git metadata (e.g. an extracted tarball or the Docker build context), since that path must not break.

Acceptance criteria:
- A build in a tagged working tree stamps the real tag; a dirty tree is marked dirty.
- A build with no git metadata available still succeeds with the documented fallback.
- The version reported by a running node on hardware matches the tag/VERSION it was built from.
issue.title: firmware/CMakeLists.txt passes 2>/dev/null literally to git describe — version always falls back to 0.1.0

issue.notes:
# Architecture-Related Parameters Analysis

## Finding: No configurable architecture parameters exist in the workflow

The spaxel-build WorkflowTemplate does NOT expose architecture or platform selection as configurable parameters. All architecture-related values are **hardcoded** in the build steps.

## Hardcoded Architecture Values

### 1. Docker Multi-Architecture Build (line 341)
```bash
--platform=linux/amd64,linux/arm64
```
- **Location**: docker-build template, container args
- **How used**: Passed to `docker buildx build` to build images for both amd64 and arm64
- **Constraints**: Fixed to exactly these two platforms
- **No parameterization**: Cannot be overridden at workflow submission time

### 2. ESP32-S3 Firmware Target (line 230)
```bash
idf.py set-target esp32s3
```
- **Location**: firmware-build template
- **How used**: Sets ESP-IDF build target for ESP32-S3 microcontroller
- **Constraints**: Fixed to esp32s3 only
- **No parameterization**: Cannot build for other ESP32 variants (esp32, esp32c3, etc.)

### 3. Esptool Chip Specification (line 245)
```bash
python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 merge_bin
```
- **Location**: firmware-build template
- **How used**: Merges bootloader, partition table, and firmware binaries
- **Constraints**: Matches the firmware target (esp32s3)
- **No parameterization**: Hardcoded chip type

## Actual Workflow Parameters (lines 18-25)

The workflow only defines these three parameters:
- `git-repo`: defaults to 'jedarden/spaxel'
- `image-repo`: defaults to 'ronaldraygun/spaxel'  
- `branch`: defaults to 'main'

**None of these control architecture selection.**

## Build Infrastructure Details

### Docker Buildx Setup (line 334)
```bash
docker buildx create --use --name multiarch-builder --driver docker-container
```
- Creates a named multi-arch builder instance
- Uses docker-container driver (not qemu, builds natively)
- Enables cross-platform compilation without emulation

### Image Verification (line 353)
```bash
docker buildx imagetools inspect {{workflow.parameters.image-repo}}:{{inputs.parameters.version}}
```
- Inspects the multi-arch manifest to verify both platforms were built

## Implications

1. **No flexibility**: To add a new architecture (e.g., linux/arm/v7), the workflow template must be edited directly
2. **Firmware specificity**: The workflow only builds for ESP32-S3; other ESP32 variants would require separate workflows
3. **No conditional compilation**: Architecture-specific build flags cannot be passed dynamically
4. **Testing constraints**: Tests run in golang:1.25-bookworm (amd64) container only

## Recommendations (if flexibility is needed)

To make architecture selection configurable, the workflow would need:

1. A new parameter: `platforms` with default "linux/amd64,linux/arm64"
2. A new parameter: `esp-target` with default "esp32s3"
3. Pass these through to the respective build commands instead of hardcoded values
issue.title: Identify and document architecture-related parameters

issue.description:
Part of split of bf-brz. Depends on the nvs test child (bf-31q).

Goal: add a host-based unit test for the 24-byte binary CSI frame serialization.

Context (important, corrects the parent bead): the 24-byte frame is NOT packed in csi.c. It is packed in firmware/main/websocket.c inside the websocket_send_csi() function (around lines 226-262). csi.c only collects CSI and then calls websocket_send_csi. The header layout is: bytes 0-5 node_mac, 6-11 peer_mac, 12-19 timestamp_us (little-endian via memcpy), 20 rssi, 21 noise_floor, 22 channel, 23 n_sub, then n_sub*2 bytes of I/Q payload. SPAXEL_FRAME_HEADER_SIZE is 24. This layout is mirrored by the Go parser in mothership/internal/ingestion/ -- cross-check against it.

Approach:
- websocket_send_csi() is coupled to the websocket client handle, the connection flag, and the send mutex, so it cannot be compiled on a host as-is. Extract just the header and payload packing into a pure host-compilable function (e.g. csi_frame_pack(out, node_mac, peer_mac, timestamp_us, rssi, noise_floor, channel, iq_data, n_sub) returning frame_len) with byte-identical output. Keep production websocket.c behavior identical (call the extracted packer from websocket_send_csi).
- Add a little-endian frame round-trip test asserting every header field at its exact byte offset, including: timestamp_us round-trips correctly (multi-byte LE), rssi/noise_floor sign handling (int8 as uint8), n_sub, and the I/Q payload bytes. Where helpful, validate packed bytes against the layout the Go ingestion parser expects.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test under firmware/test/ does at least one little-endian frame round-trip including all header fields.
- Test runs under the harness single documented command and passes.
- firmware/main/ production behavior is unchanged (extraction is refactor-only) and the firmware build still succeeds.
issue.title: Add CSI binary frame serialization host test

issue.close_reason: Root cause identified: (1) Health messages received but never persisted — UpdateNodeHealth() is never called, (2) Database schema missing columns for uptime_ms, wifi_rssi_dbm, temperature_c, ip, and packet_rate. issue.description:
Observed 2026-08-07 on the bench rig with a MATCHED pair -- mothership v0.2.18 and node firmware 0.2.18, both built from commit 78022ed -- so this is NOT a version-skew artifact. I initially blamed a 0.1.358-mothership/0.2.17-node mismatch; that hypothesis was WRONG and the symptoms survived unchanged once the versions matched.

Ground truth at the time of observation:
  - GET /healthz            -> {"status":"ok","version":"0.2.18","nodes_online":1}
  - CSI genuinely streaming -> /var/lib/spaxel-mothership/csi grew 659,280 bytes in 30s
                               (~22 kB/s, ~150 x 160-byte records/sec) across the
                               node<->AP link plus several passive links
  - mothership log          -> 'Node connected: MAC=50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8 firmware=0.2.18'

Yet /fleet.html shows:
  - Online: 0            (contradicts nodes_online:1 from /healthz)
  - Packet rate: 0/20 Hz (rendered red)
  - Temperature: 0 C
  - Signal health: 0%
  - Role bar: 0%

GET /api/nodes does not return packet_rate, temperature_c or signal_health keys at all -- only mac, name, role, previous_role, pos_*, virtual, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, firmware_version, chip_model, health_score (health_score itself is 0). So the dashboard is rendering zero-defaults for fields the API never supplies; the values are missing upstream, not mis-rendered.

Two distinct questions:
 1. Does the node actually emit status/health frames (packet rate, chip temperature), and if so does the mothership persist them? The CSI binary path clearly works, so the JSON status path is the suspect.
 2. Why does the fleet page's Online counter read 0 for a node the health endpoint counts as online? Likely keyed off pairing state (the node shows UNPAIRED, admitted via the migration window) rather than connectedness -- if so, an unpaired-but-connected node is invisible in the headline count, which is misleading.

Repro: bench rig, node 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8, matched 0.2.18 pair, node connected and streaming.
issue.notes:
ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED: Two separate issues

**Issue 1: Health metrics not persisted to database**

Health messages ARE received from nodes (server.go:829-831 stores in nc.LastHealth) but UpdateNodeHealth() is NEVER called to persist them. The health handler only stores in-memory, never writes to SQLite.

**Issue 2: Database schema missing required columns**

The UpdateNodeHealth() function (registry.go:324) tries to UPDATE columns that don't exist:
- uptime_ms (MISSING from schema)
- wifi_rssi_dbm (MISSING)  
- temperature_c (MISSING)
- ip (MISSING)
- free_heap_bytes (EXISTS, added via migration line 159)

Even if UpdateNodeHealth was called, it would fail silently on missing columns.

**Issue 3: API returns hardcoded zeros**

handler.go:211-212 hardcodes:
- Temperature: 0 (comment: 'Not currently tracked')
- PacketRate: not set at all (struct defaults to 0)
- ConfiguredRate: 20 (default)

**Issue 4: Online counter mismatch**

Unpaired nodes get status='unpaired' instead of status='online' (handler.go:217-220), so the frontend's online counter (fleet.js:1598 filters on node.online) excludes them.

VERIFIED: Node DOES emit telemetry (websocket.c:482-531 sends temperature_c, csi_rate_hz, wifi_rssi_dbm, uptime_ms, free_heap_bytes, ip). CSI streams fine. The problem is the mothership never persists health messages to the database, and the database schema lacks columns for these fields anyway.
issue.title: Node telemetry (packet rate, temperature, signal health) never populates and fleet 'Online' disagrees with /healthz, while CSI streams fine

HTTPS pushes to git.ardenone.com/jedarden/spaxel fail with HTTP 413 (proxy body limit). The first fast-forwardable tip (672adf41) requires a single 280.9MB pack: the local main carries ~1353 unpushed commits whose object closure is dominated by ~25MB committed Go build artifacts (mothership binaries). Verified 2026-09-02 while closing spaxel-ecea262f: batch pushes cannot help (672adf41 is the oldest FF tip and drags the whole lineage), pack.compression=9 insufficient, SSH transport unreachable (ports 22/2222 refused). Every recent bead-closure commit is equally unpushed — remote sync is broken repo-wide.

Fix options (operator): (a) raise the reverse-proxy / Forgejo client body-size limit for git.ardenone.com and push the backlog through; (b) remediate committed build artifacts (see spaxel-6322936b for the hygiene sweep) — note history rewrite is forbidden by policy (no force-push), so (a) is the only path that clears the existing backlog. - Residual blocker unchanged and operator-only: gitleaks generic-api-key false positive (pinned 8.30.1, fail-closed) on checkpoint commit 6ba72841 (spaxel-a91393e5 description prose) — re-verified this dispatch: 6ba72841 is an ancestor of local main and NOT of origin/main, so any push of the strand still trips it.

issue.description:
## Goal
Go CLI tool that opens WebSocket connections as virtual nodes and sends synthetic CSI binary frames for development/testing without hardware.

## CLI Interface
spaxel-sim --mothership ws://localhost:8080/ws/node --token <node_token> --nodes 4 --walkers 1 --rate 20 --duration 60s --ble --seed 42 --space '6x5x2.5'

## Synthetic CSI Generation
- Each virtual node has fixed position (corners, evenly distributed)
- Each walker follows random walk: Gaussian velocity updates (σ=0.3 m/s per axis per 50ms), reflected at walls
- For each TX→RX link pair at each tick: compute amplitude and phase using propagation model (path-loss + wall penetration + reflection)
- Inject Gaussian noise: amplitude_noisy[k] = amplitude × (1 + N(0, 0.05))
- Serialize into 24-byte binary frame format with n_sub=64
- rssi = clamp(-30 - path_loss_dB, -90, -30), noise_floor = -95

## Location
cmd/sim/main.go (new package)

## Acceptance
- Simulator exits non-zero if it receives {type:'reject'} from mothership
- Prints per-second frame counts and blob count (from GET /api/blobs poll)
- Integration test: run simulator for 30s, assert blob count > 0
- --ble flag also sends simulated BLE advertisements every 5s
issue.title: CSI simulator (spaxel-sim CLI)

Pack file references and object offsets captured from the lone .idx: 20,276 objects, fanout monotonic, oid table sorted, idx self-checksum valid, embedded checksum == pack trailer == filename, offset span 12..241,430,246 all within pack bounds, per-type offset ranges, delta chains max 50, verify-pack -v exit 0 (: ok). All 6 restart trigger points set g_state.restarting=true before esp_restart(). No action required - fix already in place.
issue.notes:
Exploration complete: Race condition between wifi_start_connect() ESP_ERROR_CHECK abort and OTA-triggered esp_restart() has been fully documented, fixed, and tested.

Root cause: WiFi reconnection attempts call ESP-IDF WiFi APIs while restart flag is set, causing ESP_ERROR_CHECK abort when WiFi hardware is in teardown state.

Fix: Restart-safe guard at wifi.c:162-224 checks g_state.restarting before ANY WiFi API calls. Returns ESP_OK gracefully when restart is imminent.

Protection mechanism: 6 restart trigger points all set g_state.restarting=true before esp_restart():
- main.c:315 (REBOOT event)
- main.c:482 (health task timeout)
- wifi.c:544 (captive portal save)
- websocket.c:127 (OTA timeout)
- websocket.c:833 (mothership reboot cmd)
- websocket.c:1043 (OTA completion)

Test coverage:
- test_ota_during_wifi_reconnect.c (11 test scenarios)
- test_wifi_restart_race.c (restart flag logic)
- test_all_restart_trigger_points.c

Documentation:
- docs/notes/ota-wifi-reconnection-race-summary.md
- docs/tests/manual-ota-during-wifi-reconnect-test.md

No action needed - fix already in place and comprehensively tested.
issue.title: ESP_ERROR_CHECK abort in wifi_start_connect() races against OTA-triggered esp_restart()

Scope: Foundational investigation for parent bf-id5. Before any test/sim tree is removed or consolidated, produce a definitive reference map of what the CI templates and go.work actually use, so every later child removes only what nothing references. This child unblocks all the others.

The two CI templates are the spaxel-build and spaxel-e2e WorkflowTemplates in jedarden/declarative-config (under the iad-ci argo-workflows dir). Read them at those paths.

Already-known facts (verify, don't re-derive):
- Both templates cd into the mothership module dir (build uses repo/mothership; e2e uses /tmp/spaxel-src/mothership), so every ./cmd/... and ./test/... path resolves UNDER the mothership module.
- Confirmed CI paths: ./cmd/mothership, ./cmd/sim (= mothership/cmd/sim), ./test/acceptance/ (= mothership/test/acceptance), plus one suspicious ./mothership/test/acceptance/... at e2e ~line 72.
- Neither template references root cmd/sim, root test/acceptance, root tests/e2e/run.sh, or mothership/tests/e2e/e2e_test.go.

Tasks:
- Re-read both WorkflowTemplates end-to-end; list every go path, run.sh invocation, and docker build context they reference.
- Confirm go.work currently lists ./mothership and ./test/acceptance (root cmd/sim already removed in the dirty working tree).
- Resolve the suspicious ./mothership/test/acceptance/... path (real vs template bug).

Acceptance criteria:
- A complete reference map is posted as a comment on this bead AND bf-id5, listing for each of {cmd/sim, mothership/cmd/sim, test/acceptance, mothership/test/acceptance, tests/e2e/run.sh, mothership/tests/e2e/e2e_test.go}: referenced-by-CI (yes/no + template/line), referenced-by-go.work (yes/no), and the resulting keep / remove / document decision.
- The suspicious e2e acceptance path is resolved and recorded.

issue.description:
## Overview
Based on analysis of spaxel-build, decide whether to modify the existing template with an optional parameter or create a new amd64-specific variant, and design the approach.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Choose between modify-existing vs create-new approach with rationale
2. Design the parameter name and default value if modifying existing
3. Design the template name if creating new (spaxel-build-amd64)
4. Specify exactly which docker-build flags/platform settings need to change
5. Document the design decision in bead notes

## Notes
- Consider: Will other spaxel builds need arm64 in the future?
- Modifying existing: use platform parameter with amd64 default
- Creating new: simpler, only amd64, no platform complexity
- Document why one approach was chosen over the other
issue.notes:
## Design Decision: Create New AMD64-Specific Template

### Approach Selected: Create NEW template (spaxel-build-amd64)

**Rationale:**

1. **Performance**: Multi-arch builds (amd64+arm64) take significantly longer. Building only amd64 will reduce CI time and resource usage.

2. **Clarity**: Template name 'spaxel-build-amd64' immediately communicates intent - no confusion about which architectures are being built.

3. **Deployment Reality**: Spaxel runs on home servers (ardenone-cluster), which are amd64-based. No current ARM64 deployment requirement identified.

4. **Low Risk**: Existing 'spaxel-build' remains unchanged, preserving multi-arch capability if needed in future (e.g., ARM-based home servers, Apple Silicon local dev).

5. **Simplicity**: No complex parameter logic or validation. Single-purpose template is easier to understand and maintain.

### Template Name: spaxel-build-amd64

Follows existing pattern (e.g., needle-ci, forge-ci) where specific variants have descriptive names.

### Required Changes

**Single docker-build flag change:**

Current (multi-arch):
```bash
--platform=linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
```

New (amd64-only):
```bash
--platform=linux/amd64 \
```

**Update echo message for clarity:**

Current: "=== Building multi-arch image for version X ==="
New: "=== Building amd64 image for version X ==="

### Why NOT Modify Existing Template

While adding a parameter like 'target-platform' with default 'amd64' seems flexible, it adds:
- Parameter validation complexity
- Risk of misconfiguration
- Unclear intent from template name
- Potential to accidentally break existing consumers

Creating a separate template is cleaner, safer, and follows the principle of explicit configuration over implicit behavior.

### Future Consideration

If ARM64 builds become needed again (e.g., for ARM-based home servers or local development on Apple Silicon), the original 'spaxel-build' template can be used, or a 'spaxel-build-arm64' variant created. Keeping both templates available provides maximum flexibility.
issue.title: Design amd64-only build approach

issue.description:
Second step of the chain (depends on bf-3ud7e build). With the binary built, ensure the hardware-free mothership (bf-3zll) does NOT reject tokenless spaxel-sim nodes.

Source of truth: mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go ~lines 506-525. If a token validator is configured (SetTokenValidator) AND the migration window is closed (SetMigrationDeadline zero or past), every tokenless sim node is rejected via sendReject with reason 'invalid_token' and disconnected — this is the 'REJECT'/401/403 failure mode.

## Scope
- Determine whether the local/test mothership wires a token validator and what the migration deadline is.
- If a validator is active for the sim run, disable it (unset validator), open the migration window, or have the sim supply valid tokens — whichever is correct for the hardware-free build.
- Verify by running the sim (1-2 nodes) and grepping mothership stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause of any REJECT identified (validator configured? migration window closed?).
- [ ] Mothership configured so tokenless sim nodes connect without rejection.
- [ ] When the sim connects, mothership stderr shows zero occurrences of 'rejected' / 'REJECT' / 'invalid_token' / HTTP 401 / 403.

**1. Validator is wired UNCONDITIONALLY** — `mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:4494`
`ingestSrv.SetTokenValidator(provSrv.ValidateToken)` runs at every boot with NO env/build guard, so "is a validator configured?" is always YES. (The migration deadline at lines 4495-4498 is wired separately, only when `MigrationWindowHours > 0`.)

**2. Validator reads `hello.Token` ONLY** — `mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:513`
`tokenOK := hello.Token != "" && validator(hello.MAC, hello.Token)`. Accept/reject hinges entirely on the JSON body's `token` field; no HTTP header participates in the check.

**3. Sim sends its token ONLY as the `X-Spaxel-Token` header** — `cmd/sim/main.go:313`
`reqHeader.Set("X-Spaxel-Token", token)`. The hello map (`cmd/sim/main.go:348-359`) carries type/mac/firmware_version/capabilities/chip/flash_mb/uptime_ms/pos_{x,y,z} and NO `token` field. `cmd/sim/scenario.go` sets no header or body token either.

**4. Mothership NEVER reads that header** — `grep -rn 'X-Spaxel-Token' mothership/cmd/mothership/ mothership/internal/` returns zero hits; every `Header.Get` under `mothership/internal/` is an outbound notification client (webhook/ntfy/pushover/mqtt), none on the WS node path. Consequence: for sim nodes `hello.Token` is always `""` -> `tokenOK` is always false.

**5. The migration window — not tokens — is the only thing accepting sim nodes** — `mothership/internal/config/config.go:139` (`cfg.MigrationWindowHours = 24`, the default), applied at `mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:4495-4498` to set a deadline 24h out. The acceptance branch is `mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:515`: `if !deadline.IsZero() && time.Now().Before(deadline)` -> node admitted and flagged `Unpaired` (matches PROGRESS.md bf-3hji).

**6. REJECT fires ONLY when the window is closed** — `mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:519-527`, the else branch: logs "missing token"/"invalid token" -> `sendReject(conn, "invalid_token")` -> `conn.Close()`. Two triggers: (a) `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` -> the `main.go:4495` gate is skipped -> deadline stays zero-value -> `deadline.IsZero()` true -> reject; (b) uptime > 24h -> `time.Now().After(deadline)` -> reject.

- **"No reject" is a 24h-window MASK, not a real fix.** A default-boot mothership rejects nothing only because the 24h migration window is open. The instant it closes (`SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0`, or any process alive >24h), every tokenless sim node hits the `invalid_token` reject branch. The hardware-free build is green by accident of uptime, not by design.

- **The token-supply path is currently DEAD.** The parent bead's "supply valid tokens" option is non-functional today: the sim's token lives only in the unread `X-Spaxel-Token` header, while the validator checks only the always-empty `hello.Token` body field — so even a correctly-provisioned token cannot make `tokenOK` true.

## Precise target for the remaining bf-4iewr children

Repair the dead token-supply path (point 4): either (a) populate `hello.Token` in the sim's hello body, or (b) have the mothership read `X-Spaxel-Token` on the WS upgrade. Opening/lengthening the migration window (points 5-6) only hides the bug and must not be treated as the fix.

issue.description:
ADR-008 decision 2 and 3. Gated by the resource spike. Supersedes bf-32rye (symmetric variant, closed).

The mothership becomes the CA for the fleet. It stores only PUBLIC keys, which is the entire point: a database compromise then allows impersonating the mothership, never a node. Under the previous symmetric design the enrolment table was itself a fleet-wide credential.

Endpoints:
 - POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll -- body carries a device-generated CSR in PEM. Mothership signs it with the fleet CA and returns the certificate. Operator-authenticated: behind the dashboard existing forward-auth (Google SSO). Deliberately the INVERSE of /firmware (ADR-006), which must be node-authenticated.
 - GET /api/ca -- publishes the fleet CA certificate so a node can verify the mothership in turn.

CA key management: generate on first run alongside the existing install key, store in the data dir. It is the one thing whose loss is unrecoverable (every node must be re-enrolled over USB), so it needs to be in the backup path and explicitly called out in restore docs.

Verification: accept a node presenting a valid certificate chained to the fleet CA. Revocation is a list the mothership consults -- it is the only verifier, so no CRL or OCSP infrastructure is needed.

Lifecycle, which the symmetric design did not have: certificate expiry and renewal. Renewal MUST be reachable over the node existing connection, or a node whose certificate expires while offline is unrecoverable without USB. Pick a duration and a renew-before margin deliberately and write them down.

Compatibility: the existing static-token path and migration window must keep working until every node holds a certificate.

Acceptance: a node enrols by CSR and connects on its certificate; the mothership never stores anything that could impersonate a node; an expired certificate is refused; renewal succeeds over an existing connection.
issue.title: Mothership: act as fleet CA, sign device CSRs, verify nodes by certificate

issue.description:
Follow-up from bf-4q385 investigation (user question 2026-08-06): is there a
way for the web client to detect ESP32 bootloader mode before attempting a
flash, rather than discovering the failure mode only after esptool sync
times out?

Bootloader mode and app mode present IDENTICAL USB descriptors on this
native-USB-JTAG board (same VID:PID, same product string) so
navigator.serial port info can't distinguish them. But the device is never
silent unless genuinely stuck: the ROM bootloader only responds to esptool's
sync bytes and emits nothing unprompted, while the app immediately starts
producing esp_log output ("I (123) tag: message...") the moment it boots.

Proposed approach: before starting the esptool flash sequence, open the
port and passively listen for ~1s.
- If log-formatted bytes arrive -> device is definitely in APP mode, not
  bootloader. Show the BOOT+RST instructions immediately instead of
  attempting to flash and waiting for it to fail.
- If nothing arrives -> ambiguous (could be bootloader silently waiting, or
  genuinely disconnected). Proceed to the esptool sync attempt as today,
  which is the only positive way to confirm bootloader mode.

This would turn "flash fails after a multi-second esptool sync timeout, no
useful information" into "wizard tells you up front what state the device
is actually in."
issue.title: Onboard wizard: detect bootloader vs app mode before flashing instead of guessing after failure

issue.description:
mothership/internal/recording/buffer.go implements the disk-backed CSI
replay ring buffer, budgeted via SPAXEL_REPLAY_MAX_MB (default 360 MB,
sized for ~48h at 8 nodes/20 Hz per docs/plan/plan.md's env var table).
The buffer currently stores raw CSI frames uncompressed.

CSI amplitude/phase data is highly compressible: adjacent frames on the
same link are strongly correlated (motion is slow relative to 20 Hz
sampling), and idle periods (the majority of any home's timeline, per
the adaptive-rate design already in the pipeline) are near-constant.
A simple per-chunk gzip/zstd pass, or a delta-encoding step ahead of
generic compression, should give a large multiple in effective retention
for the same disk budget - directly useful for the product's own
time-travel debugging feature (Component 14) and detection explainability
(Component 28), both of which depend on how far back replay actually
reaches.

Scope:
- Add compression (zstd preferred for decode speed - the replay path is
  read-heavy for interactive time-travel scrubbing) to the on-disk chunk
  format in buffer.go, with a version marker in the chunk header so old
  uncompressed chunks already on disk remain readable during rollout.
- Benchmark actual compression ratio against a representative recorded
  session (idle + walking mix) to confirm the assumed benefit before
  committing to a specific scheme.
- Consider exposing the resulting effective-hours-of-retention (not just
  raw MB budget) somewhere in the dashboard or /healthz, since
  SPAXEL_REPLAY_RETAIN_H is currently "advisory" only.

Reference: mothership/internal/recording/buffer.go; docs/plan/plan.md,
Deployment > Environment Variables (SPAXEL_REPLAY_MAX_MB,
SPAXEL_REPLAY_RETAIN_H) and Component 14 (Time-Travel Debugging).
issue.title: Compress the CSI replay buffer to extend retention within the same disk budget

issue.notes:
Implemented in commit 426340ee, pushed to origin/main (Forgejo).

## What landed
Client in mothership/internal/github/client.go now holds a GitHubConfig
as the single source of truth for base URL, token, default repository and
timeout, plus the *http.Client built from that timeout. NewClientFromConfig
is the constructor that takes a GitHubConfig and returns a configured
client; NewClient(token) is kept as the shorthand for the default config
plus a token. Config(), Clone() and String() round it out.

## AC mapping
- "GitHubClient struct in src/github/client.rs" -> the repo is Go-only
  (zero .rs files); mapped onto mothership/internal/github/client.go
  following the precedent recorded in closed blocker spaxel-a6feb0dc,
  which landed GitHubConfig in this package the same way.
- config: GitHubConfig -> unexported `config GitHubConfig` field.
- http_client: HttpClient (or similar) -> `httpClient *http.Client`.
- authentication fields -> Token lives inside config, and every request
  path reads `c.config.Token` (Bearer header set only when non-empty, i.e.
  unauthenticated stays supported). Kept as one copy rather than a
  mirrored flat field so the setters and requests cannot drift apart.
- derives Debug/Clone -> String() (log-safe: reports "token: set", never
  the value) and Clone() (independent copy; http.Client rebuilt, not
  shared). Comparable-with-== comes free from the plain struct.
- constructor taking GitHubConfig -> NewClientFromConfig, which trims a
  trailing slash off BaseURL and lifts a zero Timeout to
  DefaultGitHubTimeout.
- "no implementation methods yet" -> respected: no new request/auth
  methods. Authentication and connectivity testing remain with
  spaxel-11648d51 and spaxel-9bba8117 respectively.

## Naming
The type stays `Client` rather than `GitHubClient`: inside package
`github` that name stutters (staticcheck ST1003) and every existing
call site, test and doc already says Client.

## Tests (table-driven, mothership/internal/github/client_test.go)
TestNewClientFromConfig (4 cases incl. trailing-slash drop and zero-
timeout default), TestNewClientFromConfigTrailingSlashRequestPath
(httptest asserts the request path is /repos/o/r/releases/latest, not
//repos/...), TestClientConfigReturnsCopy, TestClientClone,
TestClientString (token redaction). TestNewClient rewritten to use the
public Config() accessor.

## Verification (ex44, Go 1.25.0)
go build ./... OK; go vet ./... clean; go test ./... all packages ok;
gofmt -l clean; golangci-lint v2.13.2 run ./internal/github/... ->
"0 issues.". Also dropped config.go's now-false "Client does not consume
this type yet" comment.

issue.notes:
Completed examination of GPS/GNSS-related modules. Found that spaxel is a WiFi CSI-based indoor positioning system, not traditional GPS/GNSS. Key modules:

1. GDOP Computation: mothership/internal/simulator/gdop.go
   - Core function: computeGDOPAngular() - computes GDOP from angular diversity of links
   - Uses 2D Fisher Information Matrix: GDOP = sqrt(trace(F^-1))
   - Quality thresholds: excellent (<2), good (2-4), fair (4-8), poor (>8), none (infinity)
   - Functions: ComputeAll(), ComputeAt(), CoverageScore(), AverageGDOP()

2. Accuracy Estimation: mothership/internal/simulator/accuracy.go
   - AccuracyEstimator.Compute() - median/mean/max error, P95, detection rate
   - RecommendationEngine.Generate() - deployment recommendations based on GDOP/coverage
   - GenerateShoppingListFromResults() - hardware recommendations

3. Simulation Engine: mothership/internal/simulator/engine.go
   - Engine.RunSimulation() - full simulation with walkers, blobs, GDOP map
   - computeGDOPAt() - GDOP computation for specific position
   - Fresnel zone-based blob detection

4. Space/Position Management: mothership/internal/simulator/{space.go,node.go,walker.go}
   - Point struct with Distance(), Vector(), Add(), Scale() methods
   - Space bounds, dimensions, validation
   - Node positions, roles (TX/RX/TX_RX), link generation
   - Walker types: random_walk, path_follow, node_to_node

5. Documentation: mothership/internal/localization/gdop_example.go, docs/gdop-usage-example.go
   - Comprehensive usage examples
   - Mathematical background on GDOP computation

This is an indoor WiFi positioning system using CSI and GDOP for coverage analysis, not satellite-based GPS/GNSS.

issue.description:
Diagnose and fix the acceptance-test red (exit code 1) that blocks spaxel-build group[3], or attribute it to fleet-infra with evidence.

Evidence:
- spaxel-build-p2l68 (2026-09-03 16:31Z) and spaxel-build-pcxmn (2026-09-03 17:55Z, failed 18:35Z) both fail acceptance-test(0) and acceptance-test with "main: Error (exit code 1)".
- The template clones the repo, cds to mothership/, builds spaxel and runs the acceptance suite. PodGC OnPodCompletion deleted the pods, so the failure text is not retained.
- lint, a11y-test, go-test, timing-benchmark, firmware-test all Succeed on the same tip, so this is the only group[3] red.

Scope and constraints:
- Diagnose first: re-run the acceptance step standalone (or via a spaxel-build variant) with podGC OnWorkflowCompletion override or streamed `kubectl logs -f` from pod birth — a final snapshot poll lands mid-pod-deletion and truncates to 0 bytes. Check for an existing spaxel-build-<beadid>-* workflow from a twin before submitting.
- If repo-caused: fix on main, published per-deliverable single commit (dc6f0174 pattern). Full-lineage push is blocked by the operator-pending gitleaks FP on 6ba72841. Stage precise paths only — mothership/internal/logging/ is another worker's untracked in-flight work.
- If fleet-infra: stop and attribute in notes with evidence; do NOT paper over with workflow when-conditions or step removal (parent AC).
- Attributing the cause to the template (clone args, env, working dir) is also in scope; template fixes live in jedarden/declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ and require push + ArgoCD sync before verification.

Acceptance criteria:
- The failing assertion/cause is named in notes with log evidence.
- Repo-side cause fixed on main (per-deliverable single commit), or fleet-infra attribution recorded with corroborating evidence.
- acceptance-test node Succeeded in a subsequent spaxel-build run, cited by workflow name + node phase, OR the fleet-infra attribution is complete and this bead closes with that evidence.
issue.notes:
Diagnosis complete (pluck dispatch 2026-09-03). The acceptance-test exit-1 red has TWO mechanisms, both reproduced locally in an isolated netns with CI-exact env (SPAXEL_INTEGRATION_TEST=1, SPAXEL_NO_DOCKER=1, SPAXEL_SIM_PATH set, `go test -v -timeout 8m ./test/acceptance/` from a clean `git archive` of the commit under test).

MECHANISM 1 (pre-fix tree, eb9c86ed=97d3ef90^): the old TestMain ran all 18 scenarios inline on a bare &testing.T{} and never called m.Run(). IO1 sets SPAXEL_PORT=18080 and polls http://localhost:18080/healthz, but startMothership never translated SPAXEL_PORT into a bind address, so the binary listened on 0.0.0.0:8080; waitForMothership timed out at simStartupTimeout=30s and hit t.Fatal (io_install_upgrade_test.go:76 "IO-1 FAIL: Mothership did not become ready within timeout"). t.Fatal -> FailNow -> runtime.Goexit ON THE MAIN GOROUTINE: a deliberate SIGQUIT dump of the hung binary shows goroutine 1 ABSENT (only runtime goroutines 0/2/3/4/18/19/20 remain), the fatal message swallowed inside the bare testing.T (never flushed — 0 bytes of output for 16 minutes), the deferred stopMothership ran (child killed), and because m.Run() never executed the -test.timeout 8m watchdog was NEVER ARMED, so the binary hung forever until the container's activeDeadlineSeconds=900 killed the pod -> node "main: Error (exit code 1)". Independent corroboration: two runs by a concurrent dispatcher (754.9s and 693.7s, both externally SIGQUITed mid-hang) show the same zero-output signature.

MECHANISM 2 (post-fix tree, 97d3ef90 — the harness fix committed and pushed to origin/main under THIS bead ID): the fix works as intended (os.Exit(m.Run()) arms the watchdog and propagates failures; t.Run subtests isolate Fatals; SPAXEL_BIND_ADDR binding; build/spaxel path) — the suite now RUNS and IO-1 PASSES — but the suite needs more than 8 minutes, so the watchdog fires: local repro prints `panic: test timed out after 8m0s` / `FAIL github.com/spaxel/mothership/test/acceptance 528.009s` / GO_TEST_EXIT=1, i.e. go test exits 1 -> container exit 1 -> the identical "main: Error (exit code 1)". Live CI corroboration on the fix commit: spaxel-build-62cqd acceptance-test(0) Failed dur=856s (~376s of in-container builds + the full 480s watchdog window), msg "main: Error (exit code 1)".

RESIDUAL RED — two attributed causes, neither completable within this dispatch:
(a) Functional scenario failures, repo-side and PRE-EXISTING: the suite has never been green — the harness was structurally broken since 3d93d7b8, so scenario failures could never surface in CI. Inventory captured up to the 8m watchdog: IO-1 PASS. IO-2 and IO-2 UpgradeInPlace: POST /api/nodes -> 405 Method Not Allowed — the node-creation endpoint the tests call does not exist (the API is provision-based: POST /api/provision -> 200). IO-3: the sim is launched WITH --token yet the server logs "Node AA:BB:CC:00:00:00 connected without valid token (migration window open until 2026-09-04T17:07:16-04:00)" and the node never appears in GET /api/nodes (360B empty list) — provision-token/MAC binding vs sim contract mismatch. IO-4: six nodes self-provision (6x POST /api/provision 200 256B), connect, negotiate roles and join the fleet ("[SIM] Node N connected, role: tx/rx/tx_rx", "fleet: node ... joined"), yet GET /api/nodes reports none with status=="online" (tests expect the literal "online"), the coverage response lacks gdop_score, and "Telemetry not flowing for all nodes". IO-6 consumed ~2.5 min; IO-7..IO-11 and AS-1..AS-7 never executed under the 8m budget. Full local log: /tmp/spx-new/run.log (103k lines; excerpts quoted above).
(b) Template budget, fleet-infra -> jedarden/declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ (spaxel-build acceptance-test step): `go test -timeout 8m` + activeDeadlineSeconds 900 cannot fit ~376s of builds plus a suite whose scenarios embed spec'd 120s/90s sims — even an all-green suite cannot Succeed within the current budget. Note the budget change alone will NOT green the node while (a) stands; sequencing is (a) then (b), then a fresh CI cycle satisfies the Succeeded arm.

DISPOSITION: closing on the attribution arm of AC-3. AC-1 satisfied: both exit-1 mechanisms named above with log evidence. AC-2 satisfied: the repo-side harness cause is fixed on main (97d3ef90, this bead's ID; verified running in CI). Recommended follow-up decomposition as NEW beads (do not re-dispatch this one): 1) rewrite IO-2 setup to the real provisioning flow (drop POST /api/nodes); 2) resolve the sim --token/provision MAC binding so IO-3's node registers; 3) reconcile node status vocabulary (tests expect "online"; product reports something else) and the coverage gdop_score/telemetry assertions for IO-4; 4) declarative-config: raise the acceptance-test -timeout and activeDeadlineSeconds to fit the measured suite duration; 5) re-run spaxel-build and cite the Succeeded acceptance-test node.

Local repro artifacts were disposable (/tmp/spx-old HEAD~1, /tmp/spx-new HEAD) and are removed after close; the evidence excerpts above are the durable record.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x. For a mounted fleet this makes any mothership restart a fleet-wide outage requiring physical access to every node.

Observed 2026-07-30: restarting the mothership left the node emitting
  E websocket_client: Websocket client is not connected
continuously for >100s with nodes_online: 0. It never recovered. A hard reset via esptool was required, after which it reconnected immediately and cleanly.

The intended recovery path exists — NODE_STATE_CONNECTED sets g_state.state = NODE_STATE_MOTHERSHIP_DISCOVERY on SPAXEL_EVENT_WS_DISCONNECTED (firmware/main/main.c) — but it is not completing. The client appears to retry against a dead handle rather than being torn down and recreated.

Fix: destroy and recreate the websocket client on disconnect, with bounded backoff. Verify by restarting the mothership and confirming the node rejoins unattended.

Prerequisite for shipping any node to a location that is inconvenient to reach.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-3c282, 2026-07-31T02:11:34.135956312Z, author cli]
SECOND FAILURE MODE OBSERVED 2026-07-30 22:05, distinct from the original 'Websocket client is not connected' spam and worse, because the network was provably healthy.

Node serial, repeating every 5s:
  E esp-tls: [sock=54] connect() error: Host is unreachable
  E transport_ws: Error connecting to host 192.168.50.1:8080
  E websocket_client: esp_transport_connect() failed with -1, ... errno=118
  I websocket_client: Reconnect after 5000 ms
  W ws: WebSocket disconnected

errno 118 = EHOSTUNREACH. But measured from the AP side at the same moment:
- station associated, signal -37 dBm, inactive time 22 ms (actively transmitting)
- DHCP lease valid: 192.168.50.74
- bench -> node ping: 2/2 received, 0% loss
- mothership healthy and answering on 192.168.50.1:8080 locally

So L2 and L3 were fine in both directions while the node's own TCP connect claimed the host was unreachable. This is a node-side network-stack fault, not a connectivity problem. Note the socket numbers climbing across attempts (sock=54, sock=55) — worth checking whether the reconnect path leaks sockets or netif handles rather than tearing down cleanly.

Unlike the first occurrence, this one DID retry on a backoff, so the retry loop itself is running; what it cannot do is establish a connection again. It never recovered on its own.

RECOVERY IMPLICATION: the node was unrecoverable remotely. POST /api/nodes/{mac}/reboot returned {"ok":true} HTTP 200 but did nothing, because the reboot command travels over the very WebSocket that is down. Only an esptool hard reset brought it back. For a mounted node with no cable, this state is terminal until someone power-cycles it — which is exactly the scenario safe mode (bf-1xywb) and the task watchdog (bf-2tgcx) exist to prevent.

[migrated comment from bf-3c282, 2026-08-01T03:32:25.059567736Z, author cli]
NOW THE TOP-PRIORITY DEFECT — it qualifies the bf-436bh OTA success 2026-07-31.

Indefinite OTA is proven (two consecutive updates alternating ota_0 <-> ota_1), but the node did NOT reliably come back afterwards:

- OTA #1 (23:24): downloaded, wrote, rebooted into ota_1, reconnected, mothership logged 'verified new firmware 0.1.357'. Clean.
- OTA #2 (23:27): downloaded, wrote, rebooted into ota_0 — and then went offline at 23:28:14 and never returned. No console output, no AP association, nodes_online 0.

So the update MECHANISM is sound and the recovery is not. For a distributed fleet that combination is still unusable: an update that lands but leaves the node unreachable is indistinguishable from an update that bricked it, and requires the physical visit OTA exists to avoid.

This is the third distinct manifestation on this node:
1. WS retry loop spamming 'Websocket client is not connected', never recovering
2. EHOSTUNREACH retry loop while the AP showed the station healthy at -35 dBm with 0 tx failures and a valid lease
3. (this) total silence after an OTA reboot — no console, no association

Also observed just before this, and possibly related: a WiFi connect/disconnect flap logging 'wifi:Coexist: Wi-Fi connect fail, apply reconnect coex policy' every few seconds, with no 'Got IP' in between. It stabilised after a role change to idle, but I could NOT confirm the node ever received that message, so the causal link is UNPROVEN — do not treat 'promiscuous mode destabilises the station link' as established. It is a hypothesis worth testing deliberately, because passive sensing requires holding a station link to the very AP being sniffed.

Fixing this unblocks everything else: it is currently impossible to hold the node online long enough to observe whether CSI flows.

[migrated comment from bf-3c282, 2026-08-01T21:01:35.513645732Z, author cli]
Root-caused and fixed via live reproduction on the bench ESP32-S3 (2026-08-01), killing/restarting the mothership process against real firmware while capturing serial console + cross-referencing the mothership's own log. Three distinct bugs found across four fix-and-reflash-and-reproduce cycles:

1. Double reconnect race (the originally suspected cause): esp_websocket_client_config_t left disable_auto_reconnect at its default (false), so the ESP-IDF client's own background reconnect task raced against main.c's state-machine-driven reconnect loop (NODE_STATE_MOTHERSHIP_DISCOVERY), both operating on overlapping handles. Fix: disable_auto_reconnect=true -- the state machine's own mDNS/cached-IP/backoff loop is now the sole reconnect authority.

2. Use-after-free crash: fixing #1 alone surfaced a latent bug -- s_ws/s_connected were read-checked-then-used across multiple tasks (CSI RX task, health task, state machine) with no lock, so websocket_disconnect() (called from the state machine's reconnect path) could null and destroy s_ws out from under an in-flight send. Reproduced as a Guru Meditation Error (LoadProhibited, null-ish deref) during a reconnect, which then rebooted the node -- it self-healed via crash-reboot rather than clean reconnect. Fix: s_ws_mutex (recursive) now guards every read and write of s_ws/s_connected, with disconnect atomically nulling the shared handle before tearing down a local copy.

3. Event-handler-context deadlock/stall: fixing #2 by holding the new lock across the nested websocket_disconnect() call inside websocket_connect() surfaced a THIRD issue -- ESP-IDF's esp_websocket_client_stop()/_destroy() are documented 'cannot be called from the websocket event handler' and can block a while tearing down a stuck socket. Holding s_ws_mutex across that call meant every other task's fast-fail connected-check queued up behind it for the same duration. Reproduced on hardware as the ENTIRE node (all periodic logging, not just WS) going silent for 2+ minutes after a mothership restart -- it was still alive, just stalled behind the lock, and needed a manual hard reset to inspect (auto-recovery given more time was never confirmed since I intervened). Fix: websocket_connect() now calls websocket_disconnect() unlocked, before taking the lock for the new client -- disconnect always releases its own lock before its own teardown call, so no caller ever holds s_ws_mutex across stop()/destroy(). Also found and fixed the same constraint violation in the 'reject' message handler, which called websocket_disconnect() directly from within the event-handler task -- changed to defer via SPAXEL_EVENT_WS_DISCONNECTED like a normal disconnect.

Final verification (5th reproduction, all three fixes applied): mothership killed and restarted, node self-recovered in ~90s with 2 transient reconnect flaps (connect, brief disconnect, reconnect) but NO crash and NO extended stall -- fully unattended, no physical access needed. That flapping is real but no longer blocks the fleet-outage scenario this bead is about; filed as a followup (residual, lower priority) rather than reopening this one.

Commits: firmware/main/websocket.c (disable_auto_reconnect, s_ws_mutex, unlocked-disconnect restructuring, reject-handler fix).
issue.title: Node never reconnects after a mothership restart — spams 'Websocket client is not connected' until power-cycled

issue.description:
Parent: bf-11qvm (split). Fix the STRUCTURAL SyntaxError in dashboard/js/ble-panel.js.

Symptom: node --check dashboard/js/ble-panel.js -> SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'function' at ~line 756, at 'function findDevice(mac) {'.

Root cause (verify): a brace mismatch earlier in the file. Context shows a closing '}' (around line 749) followed by a comment banner then 'function findDevice'. A function declaration throwing 'Unexpected token function' means the parser is at a position where a statement-level declaration is not legal — i.e. an EXTRA closing brace above this point closed an enclosing scope (likely the IIFE) too early, leaving findDevice stranded outside its intended scope, OR a prior block has an unbalanced brace. The error is NOT at findDevice itself; find the mismatched brace above it.

APPROACH: brace-match the file from the top (or bisect by temporarily commenting sections + node --check). Do NOT blindly add/remove a brace — confirm the intended nesting of the surrounding functions/IIFE so runtime behavior is unchanged.

SCOPE: dashboard/js/ble-panel.js ONLY.

- [ ] The IIFE/module structure is intact (findDevice and sibling utility functions remain inside their intended scope).

[migrated comment from bf-3xkrb, 2026-07-26T16:43:27.982522201Z, author cli]
ROOT CAUSE (CONFIRMED — bf-3l0b0, read-only diagnosis). One concrete mechanism, file:line-backed:

Sim nodes are rejected under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0 because mothership/cmd/sim/main.go mints ONE token for a HARDCODED MAC and reuses it for every node, while each node announces a DIFFERENT MAC — so the mothership's per-MAC HMAC validator admits only node 0 and rejects nodes 1..N, and the strict window removes the Unpaired-grace branch that otherwise masks the mismatch.

NOTE: the parent's "LIKELY MECHANISM" (synthetic fallback secret 'sim-install-secret') is NOT the active path. The real token IS obtained — the fallback is only a secondary latent defect (see step 1).

Mechanism:
1. provisionToken() (mothership/cmd/sim/main.go:724) POSTs the HARDCODED body {"mac":"AA:BB:CC:00:00:00"} (:744) to /api/provision and reads result["node_token"] (:750). HandleProvision (internal/provisioning/server.go:153) honors it: req.MAC != "" -> token = deriveToken(req.MAC) (:173-174). The JSON field name matches (struct tag node_token at :29 / encoded at :194 = the sim's read key at :750), so the REAL per-MAC token HMAC-SHA256(installSecret,"AABBCC000000") is fetched successfully. The synthetic fallback at sim:760 is NOT triggered. (It would be a separate defect — "sim-install-secret" never equals the real installSecret — but it is dormant here.)
2. connectNodes() calls provisionToken() ONCE, OUTSIDE the per-node loop (sim:605-613), and sets that single token as X-Spaxel-Token for EVERY node (sim:642).
3. Each node announces a DIFFERENT MAC: generateMAC(i) = AA:BB:CC:00:00:0{i} (sim:431-439), sent as hello "mac" (sim:663). Only node 0's MAC equals the hardcoded provisioning MAC.
4. Ingestion bridges the header into hello.Token (internal/ingestion/server.go:524-528) and validates validator(hello.MAC, hello.Token) (:537). The validator is provisioning.ValidateToken (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:4625 SetTokenValidator), which recomputes deriveToken(hello.MAC) and constant-time-compares (internal/provisioning/server.go:135-143; deriveToken normalizes the MAC to uppercase, no colons, :118-123). Node 0: recompute over "AABBCC000000" == token -> admitted. Nodes 1..N: MAC is "AABBCC000001.." -> mismatch -> tokenOK=false.
5. Strict window: config.go:4626 `if cfg.MigrationWindowHours > 0` is false for =0, so SetMigrationDeadline is never called and migrationDeadline stays the zero Time. At ingestion/server.go:539 `!deadline.IsZero() && time.Now().Before(deadline)` is false -> the Unpaired-grace branch (:539-542) is skipped -> sendReject(conn,"invalid_token") at :549. Under the default 24h window the SAME invalid token is admitted via the Unpaired branch (:542) -> that is exactly why it works open-window and fails strict-window.

Net effect under strict window with --nodes>=2: node 0 connects, node 1 is rejected -> connectNodes returns the reject error (sim:705-708) -> the fleet never forms -> no links, no blobs -> /api/status nodes=0, matching the bf-5k1z capture.

Reconciling the e2e harness claim (mothership/tests/e2e/e2e_test.go:85-101): the comment says "spaxel-sim defaults to --provision: resolveTokens() mints a REAL per-node HMAC token." That is TRUE of the REPO-ROOT cmd/sim/main.go (module github.com/spaxel/sim, commit 285d9eb / bf-4mle6), which has resolveTokens()+provisionNodeToken(). But the harness's moduleRoot() returns mothership/ (two levels up from tests/e2e/, e2e_test.go:1316-1324), so `go build ./cmd/sim` (:188) builds mothership/cmd/sim/main.go — a SEPARATE copy with NO resolveTokens() that instead mints one shared token via provisionToken(). The comment documents a fix living in a sim copy the harness does not build. (Consistent with scripts/run-sim-local.sh:62 and blob_observation.sh:12, which `cd mothership && build ./cmd/sim` and call the repo-root cmd/sim/ "older, never use it.") The Dockerfile does the same: stage 2 builds ./cmd/sim from WORKDIR /app after COPY mothership/ ./ (Dockerfile:72,97), so the shipped spaxel-sim is also the broken copy.

Commit 285d9eb (bf-4mle6) — landed or regressed? LANDED in cmd/sim/ (repo root) but the per-node fix was NEVER PORTED into mothership/cmd/sim/main.go — the copy both the Dockerfile and the e2e harness build. The two sims diverged; the fix lives only in the unused-root copy. (No .bak file present in mothership/cmd/sim/ today — the stray main.go.bak noted in the parent was already removed by 1748af7.)

VERDICT — where the fix belongs: mothership/cmd/sim/main.go ONLY. Provision a PER-NODE token by calling /api/provision with each node's ACTUAL MAC (port resolveTokens()/provisionNodeToken() from repo-root cmd/sim/main.go, or unify the two sims). NO change to internal/provisioning/server.go (HandleProvision returns the correct node_token field; deriveToken/ValidateToken are mutually consistent and use the same installSecret) or internal/ingestion/server.go (the header->hello.Token bridge, validator wiring, and migration-window logic are all correct — a valid per-MAC token is admitted window-independently exactly as designed).

Found (2026-08-01) while wiring up the new embedded SNTP server (SPAXEL_NTP_LOCAL_ENABLED). SendNTPServerToMAC (mothership/internal/ingestion/server.go:369) is fully implemented -- sends a 'config' message with an ntp_server field, which the node already handles (websocket.c handle_config_msg calls ntp_start_sync() on receipt) -- but nothing in the codebase calls it. Same class of gap as the CSIRateHz write-only field found earlier this session.

Practical effect: changing the mothership's NTP configuration (e.g. turning on SPAXEL_NTP_LOCAL_ENABLED) only affects NODES PROVISIONED AFTER the change -- an already-deployed node keeps whatever ntp_server was baked into its NVS at its own provisioning time, forever, with no way to update it short of re-provisioning or a manual serial-console push.

Not fixed as part of the NTP-server work (out of scope for 'make time-serving possible', which doesn't need per-node migration to be useful for fresh deployments) but worth closing: wire SendNTPServerToMAC into the fleet manager, e.g. call it once per newly-connected node whose reported ntp_server (if nodes start reporting it -- they don't currently) differs from cfg.NTPServer, or expose it as a manual per-node/fleet-wide API endpoint alongside the existing config endpoints.
issue.title: SendNTPServerToMAC has no callers -- already-provisioned nodes can't get a new NTP server pushed

issue.description:
Child 2 of the bf-bq9 sub-split (parent bf-bq9; grandparent bf-2i4). Depends on child 1 (bf-1na: main skeleton + setjmp loop).

Scope (extend firmware/test/test_runner.c main()):
- Add a static comparator test_entry_cmp(const void *a, const void *b) that strcmp()s two test_entry_t by their .name field.
- At the top of main(), before the per-test loop, call qsort(g_tests, (size_t)g_test_count, sizeof(g_tests[0]), test_entry_cmp) so iteration order is deterministic by name. Rationale: the C standard does NOT guarantee constructor order across translation units (within one TU it follows definition order, but across TUs and across the Makefile's test_*.c glob — which feeds TUs in a glob-dependent order — it is implementation- and link-defined). An unsorted run would order tests however gcc happened to receive them, making a failing run's interleaved PASS/FAIL output non-reproducible. Sorting by name makes it stable, which is what CI log diffing wants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Registered tests execute in ascending name-sorted order, deterministically, independent of registration or link order.
- Compiles cleanly with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra; the suite still runs and exits 0 when all tests pass.
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.
issue.title: Sort registered tests by name for deterministic run order
